Sports.title: EFL 2026-27 predictions with Championship winners decided as West Ham and Wolves discover fate
Sports.content:
Forgive me for going full Jamie O'Hara here, but it's time to rejoice: proper football is BACK.

Yes, last week's Carabao Cup games - and the World Cup - were a nice little distraction to tide us over but the real stuff is back this weekend. And there's plenty of talking points to get stuck into before we prepare to embark on the white-knuckle ride that is a 46 game EFL season.

In the Championship, it's the land of the fallen giants with West Ham, Wolves and Burnley dropping back into the second tier. Will they make an instant return? Or can the teams who narrowly missed out on promotion last year, such as Middlesbrough, Millwall and Southampton, beat them to the post? Don't forget, the top eight will make up the play-offs this year.

Then in League One, Leicester City are the big scalp after dropping into arguably the most unpredictable division of all. They will vie with Sheffield Wednesday and Jack Wilshere's Luton Town for promotion. And in League Two, can Gary Neville and David Beckham's Salford City finally get over the line after some eye-catching transfer business?

‌



Nobody really knows. But Mirror Football's crack team have taken a stab at predicting the big winners and losers...

James Whaling

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Wolves

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: Portsmouth

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

It's hard to see West Ham not making an immediate return to the top flight. Keeping hold of Jarrod Bowen is an unbelievable bit of business and their squad should be far too strong for the second tier. Middlesbrough look ready to join them in the Premier League after another near-miss last term, somehow managing to lose twice in the playoffs. I fancy Wolves to also bounce straight back, fired by the goals of the returning Raul Jimenez.

At the wrong end of the league, I think Blackburn may sail too close to the sun one too many times and slip into the third division. Charlton look set for another season of struggle and, as well as Lincoln have done reaching the Championship, I think they may find it difficult.

Portsmouth have made some shrewd additions in the transfer window and will be strong at home. Manager John Mousinho has another season of Championship experience under his belt and I think they may surprise a few.

‌



Leicester, similarly to West Ham, have a squad far too strong for the level they are playing at and should bounce straight back to the Championship. Gary Neville, David Beckham and Salford City to win League Two.

View 6 Images Jarrod Bowen and West Ham are the red-hot favourites to win the Championship (Image: Rob Newell/CameraSport)

Ben Husband

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

‌



Relegated: Bolton, Lincoln, Blackburn

Top scorer: Raul Jimenez

Surprise package: QPR

League One winners: Leicester

‌



League Two winners: Salford

I know what you’re thinking…way to go out on a limb. The Championship prediction is made with more than a hint of bias, but I do think if Wolves can get one or two more faces through the door before the window closes they could be formidable. Simply put, a squad including Andre, Kieran Trippier, Raul Jimenez, Mateus Mane and Adam Armstrong should be enough to get it done. Even with some fierce competition from the likes of West Ham, Middlesbrough and Southampton - who will miss out due to their points deduction.

In League One, despite how disastrous his Rangers reign was, Russell Martin is a more than good enough manager to get Leicester back into the Championship. Although they will need to start well to arrest the slide that is now two years in the making.

And in League Two, the arrivals of Macauley Langstaff and Luke Molyneux - to a side that made the play-off final last season - should be enough for Salford City.

‌



Dan Marsh

Championship winners: Wolves

Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich

Relegated: Bolton, Charlton, Lincoln

Top scorer: Will Lankshear

‌



Surprise package: Cardiff City

League One winners: Luton Town

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

Everyone is having West Ham as the bankers to win the league but I'm not convinced Nuno Espirito Santo's pragmatic approach necessarily translates into a top two finish. Their squad is a joke, though, while and they'll be amongst the top teams, clubs will relish the prospect of going to the London Stadium and claiming a major scalp. The scrutiny on West Ham should open the door for Wolves to mount a title challenge with slightly less pressure. They have a manager who has no Championship experience but their squad, too, does not belong at this level and they are my picks for the title. Middlesbrough have levelled up in key areas, namely in goal (Radek Vitek over Sol Brynn) and up front, where Will Lankshear should feast if Boro can repeat the buffet of chances they produced for their forwards last season. I fancy them to finish second with Norwich, resurgent after appointing Philippe Clement midway through the season, a force in the play-offs.

‌



At the other end of the table, Bolton and Charlton have had underwhelming transfer windows. Bolton will be right up against it after coming up through the play-offs, while Charlton, who eventually got over the line last season after winning the previous year's play-offs, have not signed the creative players required for them to 'evolve' as Nathan Jones wishes. Lincoln City have momentum and the nucleus of the squad that destroyed League One last year but losing Michael Skubala and their best player, Jack Moylan, makes an already daunting task even more difficult. Cardiff City are my surprise package tip; I fancy Brian Barry-Murphy's expansive style will translate well to the Championship and star striker Yousef Salech will also handle the step up with aplomb.

Everybody is tipping Leicester to romp League One so I'll go against the curve and tip Luton; they finished the season strongly after winning the EFL Trophy and Jack Wilshere will be all the better for the experience. Salford City have done some eye-catching business and again are heavily fancied to win League Two but Steve Evans has rebuilt Bristol Rovers and I can see them being there or thereabouts under him.

View 6 Images Wolves are likely to be among the teams vying for promotion (Image: David Rogers)

Felix Keith

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Norwich City

Relegated: Portsmouth, Cardiff, QPR

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

It really is hard to look past West Ham. Nuno Espirito Santo has been there and done it and, as many have pointed out, Bowen is far too good for the Championship. Something will have to go very wrong for the Hammers to mess it up. Southampton have (so far) managed to hold onto their best players, barring Shea Charles, so should be right in the mix for promotion again. But Tonda Eckert still has an FA charge hanging over his head, which could prompt a lengthy touchline ban. The fallout from Spygate could cost them and help Middlesbrough.

Norwich were a team transformed after Philippe Clement’s arrival last season. They’re only eighth favourites with the bookies for promotion but I can see them surprising a few.

‌



Portsmouth and QPR survived last season but were largely dreadful and could help Lincoln stay up after promotion from League One.

I fancy Russell Martin to get Leicester back up, despite losing some exciting players and the financial might behind the Salford project can’t afford it to stall much longer.

Samuel Meade

Championship winners: West HamPromoted: Middlesbrough, MillwallRelegated: Watford, Bolton, CardiffTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: LincolnLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Port Vale The Hammers keeping hold of Nuno Espirito Santo and Jarrod Bowen is their two best bits of business and they'll have too much not to return immediately. Lincoln as a surprise may raise eyebrows, given they won League One with more than 100 points, but plenty have tipped them for the drop.

Leicester are an obvious contender for League One and I'm not convinced by Salford in League Two, despite them being promotion favourites.

‌



View 6 Images New boy Will Lankshear will spearhead Middlesbrough's bid for promotion (Image: Trevor Wilkinson/NurPhoto)

Jeremy Cross

Championship winners: Southampton

Promoted: West Ham, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Watford, Stoke, Charlton

‌



Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Millwall

League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Bristol Rovers

‌



Southampton have a lot to prove to the game and themselves this season, following their shameful end to the last one. But getting caught spying on play-off opponents Middlesbrough will give the Saints more than enough fuel to come back fighting again, only this time legally, hopefully. Despite his dubious approach and the subsequent four point deduction, manager Tonda Eckert has done a fine job on the south coast. The season-long loan signing of striker Divin Mubama from Manchester City could prove to be a shrewd move, while the arrival of Lewis Dobbin from Aston Villa in a £10m deal will bring some class and composure to the team.

Middlesbrough have been promotion contenders for a few seasons now, and have only finished outside the top eight once since 2022, so this could well be their time to make a return to the top flight. West Ham, meanwhile, have kept hold of their two best assets despite relegation from the Premier League, in the shape of manager Nuno Santo and England international Jarrod Bowen. Bowen is too good for the Championship, and should be the best player in the entire league this season. If he can maintain the form he's capable of, his goals should give the Hammers an immediate return to the top flight.

Leicester still have the quality to get back into the Championship from League One, while Bristol Rovers look to be the best placed team to win League Two ahead of Salford City.

Brian Dick

Championship winners: West Ham United

‌



Promoted: Middlesbrough, Southampton

Relegated: Lincoln City, Bolton Wanderers, Blackburn Rovers

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Norwich City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Barnet

West Ham are the most obvious Championship winners since Newcastle United came down a few years ago. In Nuno they have a proven manager who has won the league before, Jarrod Bowen who will be the best player in the division and a financial muscle and set-up that separates them from the field.

Middlesbrough were the best team in the league for so long last season but ran out of goals, a shortcoming they look to have addressed. Tonda Eckert may have landed in hot water but if he survives any sanction after Spygate, it was clear he had the Saints on the charge last term. Norwich also came like a train after the appointment of Philippe Clement and have recruited well.

‌



Leicester will be too strong not to bounce back from League One, as long as they keep their noses clean on the financial front. Barnet look well-placed to improve on last season’s eighth.

View 6 Images Russell Martin will lead Leicester City in League One (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC)

Peter Smith

Championship winners: West Ham

Promoted: Southampton

‌



Relegated: Lincoln, Bolton, Portsmouth

Top scorer: Taty Castellanos

Surprise package: Stoke City

League One winners: Leicester City

‌



League Two winners: Salford City

The relegated three might have endured varying levels of chaos on their way back to the Championship but their squads should still be strong enough to set the pace. Then again, Southampton had the best squad last year and it took until they changed manager to show it. Even with a points deduction, a couple of key departures and the disdain of their rivals they will be around about it this time.

It is going to be so tight between most of the rest and it will come down to who has a knack of tipping close games in their favour. Stoke’s chances of a good year at last hang on an overhauled midfield. Most seasons since 2018 have all-but finished in January so, with the play-off expansion, it would be a dream for supporters to go into the spring feeling alive.

Leigh Curtis

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves (second), Norwich (playoffs)

Relegated: Portsmouth, Blackburn, Bolton

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Lincoln City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford City

West Ham's squad is just too good to be at this level for any longer than a season. Keeping Jarrod Bowen was huge and Nuno, despite relegation last season, is still a good and wily manager. I can't see beyond them for the title and I still expect them to strengthen in the transfer market too. It would be a huge shock if they didn't win it. Wolves have made a couple of impressive signings and I fully expect them to be challenging West Ham for the crown. César Peixoto is new to English football, but he looks to have them better organised from what I've seen in pre-season. Plus they aren't finished in the market. As for the playoffs, I was hugely impressed by Norwich last season towards the back end of the campaign. Had a good run under Phillipe Clement. I like the Andre Brooks signing and their forwards are a real handful. I'm predicting them to go up at Wembley. I love Tony Mowbray, but I think he's got his hands full at Blackburn in trying to keep them in the league this season. The signings haven't really caught the eye and there's still problems that need resolving. Portsmouth I thought would go down last year, but they had a decent run towards the back end of the campaign that got them out of trouble, but I think this might be the year. And Bolton I think could be in danger purely because the first season out of League One is always tough because the leap from that to the Championship is vast.

View 6 Images Former Millwall man Macaulay Langstaff will lead the line for League Two promotion hopefuls Salford City this season (Image: Harriet Massey)

‌



Lincoln may well surprise a few people this year. They have a unique way of playing, but they are well organised, their excellent at set-pieces and their pressing is very good. In Ben House they have an absolute machine who never stops running. Sincil Bank is not the easiest place to visit either.

Top scorer is a tough one to call but I am going to say Jarrod Bowen, although I think Mohamed Toure at Norwich and Adam Armstrong at Wolves will run him very close.

In League One, I just think Leicester will be too strong for the division really. Once they get acclimatised the division, they should bounce back straight back. Salford have had an excellent summer of recruitment in the division below and Macualey Langstaff will score bundles at that level. Unbelievable signing for the level.

Tom Coleman

Championship winners: West Ham

‌



Promoted: Wolves, Middlesbrough

Relegated: Lincoln, Charlton, Blackburn

Top scorer: Jarrod Bowen

Surprise package: Swansea City

‌



League One winners: Leicester City

League Two winners: Salford

West Ham have to be favourites to go back up to the Premier League as champions. They've got such a strong squad for this level and I strongly suspect Jarrod Bowen will tear up the division and score loads of goals. Last season's Golden Boot winner Zan Vipotnik will also hope to be in the mix. Middlesbrough really impressed me under Kim Hellberg and I suspect they'll be an even better prospect this time around. Wolves also look to be firmly in the hunt.

At the other end, I think Lincoln will find the step up just a bit too much, but I think Cardiff City and Bolton might just have enough for some reason. Charlton and Blackburn just about escaped last time out but I think they might just struggle this time around.

‌



As for the surprise package, I really like what Swansea have done this summer. They've strengthened in key areas and if they can keep hold of Vipotnik they'll have three top forwards for this level with Adam Idah and Ross Stewart also on the books. I wouldn't be at all surprised if they're part of the play-off conversation.

Nathan Ridley

Championship winners: Middlesbrough

Promoted: West Ham, WolvesRelegated: Lincoln, Charlton, PrestonTop scorer: Jarrod BowenSurprise package: NorwichLeague One winners: LeicesterLeague Two winners: Chesterfield

I can't see any spying from stopping Middlesbrough this year, with Kim Hellberg having made quality additions in key areas over the summer. I'm then backing West Ham to finish second with their stacked squad - hence my pick for top scorer, Jarrod Bowen - and Wolves to win the play-offs.

‌



Going down, I don't see Lincoln's managerial setup working while I think Charlton and Preston's boardroom uncertainty will permeate onto the pitch. Norwich, meanwhile, are almost in danger of the dark horse curse given the amount of fans and pundits tipping them for a play-off finish.

In League One, I can't look past Leicester. And I'll go with Chesterfield for the League Two title - it genuinely would've been York had they not sacked Stuart Maynard.

Sports.title: Man Utd signing Myles Lewis-Skelly would be bad news for seven players
Sports.content:
Man Utd signing Myles Lewis-Skelly would be bad news for seven players

Manchester United signing Arsenal defender Myles Lewis-Skelly this summer could be a serious coup - but it could also create a few problems for Michael Carrick's side

View 6 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on his way to Man Utd (Image: Getty Images)

Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on his way to Manchester United, which may spell bad news for several Red Devils stars. The 19-year-old Arsenal starlet, who can play at both left back and in central midfield, has been placed on the transfer list after falling out of favour under Mikel Arteta last season.

‌



Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both United and Chelsea, with Arsenal valuing him at around £45 million. Despite emerging as one of the most exciting talents to come through the Gunners' academy in years, Arsenal are willing to cash in as they look to recoup some of the £75m they spent on Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



United appear to be his most likely destination, with Michael Carrick's side actively searching for a new midfielder and left back. They had initially identified Lewis Hall as their top target, but Newcastle's refusal to sell has forced them to explore alternatives.

‌



Lewis-Skelly would undoubtedly plug a major gap in Carrick's squad, but his arrival could also create some problems too. With that in mind, here are seven Manchester United players who could find themselves worse off if the Arsenal youngster moves to Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Paul Pogba set to have contract torn up as injured ex-Man Utd star searches for new club READ MORE :

Man Utd have clear transfer priority after Myles Lewis-Skelly offer READ MORE :

Luke Shaw

With his contract expiring next year, Luke Shaw's days at Manchester United appear to be numbered. But the arrival of Lewis-Skelly could make what's shaping up to be his final season at Old Trafford a frustrating one, with regular first-team football potentially harder to come by.

‌



Shaw would presumably drop to second choice at left back, despite arguably enjoying his most consistent campaign in years. The 31-year-old featured in all 38 Premier League matches last season for the first time in his injury-hit career, making a sudden fall down the pecking order a harsh outcome.

However, signing a player of Lewis-Skelly's ability and potential would be a clear indication that United are planning for the future - and Shaw could be one of the biggest casualties of that long-term thinking.

View 6 Images Luke Shaw would likely be bumped to second-choice left back if Myles Lewis-Skelly signs (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Patrick Dorgu

Patrick Dorgu's first-team opportunities could also take a hit following Lewis-Skelly's arrival, even though the Denmark international has recently been operating in a more advanced role.

Dorgu originally joined United from Lecce as a wing-back under Ruben Amorim, but his role changed after Carrick took charge, with the 21-year-old increasingly used on the left wing. He can still provide cover at left back, but that versatility may not be enough to guarantee regular football.

With United already boasting plenty of attacking options - and with both Lewis-Skelly and Shaw ahead of him in the left back pecking order - Dorgu could find himself fighting for minutes at both ends of the pitch next season.

‌



View 6 Images Dorgu's Manchester United future would be under serious threat if Lewis-Skelly joins (Image: Getty Images)

Kobbie Mainoo

Despite playing most of his senior football as a left back, Lewis-Skelly shone as a central midfielder at the back end of last season. That could be particularly bad news for Kobbie Mainoo, who was handed something of a new lease on life after Carrick's arrival and was restored to the starting XI.

Mainoo's place in the team is far from guaranteed, though, as we saw under Amorim, and Lewis-Skelly could pose a serious threat to his position if he can replicate the form he showed in midfield for Arsenal.

‌



The pair have a similar profile, offering energy, technical ability, ball-carrying skills and versatility to operate in different areas of the pitch. If Lewis-Skelly adapts quickly and impresses in the middle of the park, Mainoo could once again find himself fighting for a starting spot at Old Trafford.

View 6 Images Kobbie Mainoo has been in and out of Manchester United's first team over the past year or so (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Manuel Ugarte

Manuel Ugarte already looks to have fallen out of Manchester United's first-team picture, and the arrival of Lewis-Skelly could be the final nail in the coffin for the midfielder's Old Trafford career.

‌



Carrick's side have already strengthened their midfield with the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans this summer, while Lewis-Skelly would provide another option capable of playing centrally. With plenty of alternatives at the manager's disposal, Ugarte could find himself pushed even further down the pecking order.

The Uruguayan was expected to leave this summer, but those plans were put on hold after he suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup. Even once he returns to full fitness, though, regular minutes could be even harder to come by if Lewis-Skelly joins.

View 6 Images Manuel Ugarte's United future looks uncertain (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Diogo Dalot

Though predominantly a right back, Diogo Dalot's first-team opportunities could also take a knock if Lewis-Skelly signs.

The Portugal international is capable of operating on either flank, but his chances of starting at left back or left wing back would be severely reduced with Lewis-Skelly and Shaw potentially ahead of him in the pecking order.

Dalot's main competitor for minutes is Noussair Mazraoui, but Lewis-Skelly's arrival would create something of a log-jam in defence. And with several players capable of filling multiple positions, regular game time could become increasingly difficult to come by for everyone.

‌



View 6 Images Diogo Dalot could have some unwanted extra competition at full back (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

Diego Leon and Harry Amass

Then there is the impact Lewis-Skelly could have on two of United's most promising young left-back prospects, Diego Leon and Harry Amass. Both youngsters are regarded as players with the potential to break into the first team, but a move for Lewis-Skelly could make that pathway considerably more difficult.

The Arsenal star's arrival would give United an established young option at left-back, potentially leaving Leon and Amass to battle for scraps or wait even longer for their opportunity.

Article continues below

United will not want to block the development of two highly rated academy prospects, but signing Lewis-Skelly could do exactly that. If he establishes himself as the long-term answer at left back, the route into the first team for Leon and Amass would suddenly become a whole lot harder.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola set to be handed new transfer priority as double update emerges

Liverpool's stuttering summer transfer window could about to become even more complicated

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is looking to add to his squad this summer (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

Liverpool could be facing another transfer headache this summer. The window slams shut on September 1 and the Reds are still scrambling to get a mega-money deal over the line for PSG winger Bradley Barcola.

‌



Andoni Iraola's priority has been bolstering Liverpool's attack, namely securing a replacement for Mohamed Salah, and supplementing their forward line as a whole. However, the Reds are now braced for interest in two of their own midfielders.

‌



The updates mean Liverpool's Basque head coach may now have to pivot his attentions to strengthening his engine room. This would no doubt be a monumental task given that the Reds' hierarchy are still focusing their energies on the last third of the pitch.

‌



Alexis Mac Allister interest

Liverpool are braced for interest in Alexis Mac Allister this summer. Galatasaray have lodged their interest in recruiting the 27-year-old, according to reports in Turkey.

That interest has so far been declared via intermediaries to determine a price and the Argentine's wage demands, according to Yeni Asir. However, that's not all.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



According to talkSPORT, Manchester City have also shortlisted the World Cup-winner as they look to replace Rodri, who could be on his way to Barcelona this summer. However, the report stresses that there's been "no contact or developments" on any deal to take the midfielder to Manchester.

Mac Allister has been a regular in the Reds' midfield since his arrival from Brighton in 2023. However, he has now entered the final two years of his Anfield contract and suffered a dip in form last season, which saw him touted for an exit this summer.

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



Should he leave, Iraola would have to refocus his energies on replacing the star, with the Reds currently relying on Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai as three of his senior midfielders. Harvey Elliott, Trey Nyoni, Wataru Endo and Stefan Bajcetic are also options, but all except Nyoni have also been linked with an exit this summer.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta eyes Barcelona raid as £85m star opens door to transfer

Mikel Arteta is eager to improve his Arsenal squad ahead of the new Premier League season

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta continues plotting Arsenal's next move in the transfer market (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta remains focused on bolstering his Arsenal squad before the summer transfer window closes. The Premier League champions begin their title defence in eight days against Coventry City, but first face Manchester City on Sunday in the Community Shield.

‌



Despite missing out on Vinicius Junior after he signed a contract extension with Real Madrid, the Gunners acquired his international team-mate Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in a £75million deal.

‌



The 28-year-old's arrival marked Arsenal's fourth summer signing, but plans to add further remain among Arteta's priorities. The north London side are said to be targeting a Barcelona star, while an £85m-rated player has opened the door to an England move.

‌



Barcelona target emerges

Arsenal have attempted to sign defensive reinforcements this summer, but to no avail. William Saliba's absence for "an extended period" leaves Arteta without one of his best defenders ahead of the new season.

The Premier League champions have been interested in Aston Villa star Ezri Konsa but are set to turn their attention to Barcelona defender Jules Kounde, if the France international opens the door to a possible move, Spanish outlet Sport reports.

Tottenham could hand Arsenal major transfer boost after opening Folarin Balogun talks READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The outlet claims that Arsenal are looking for a centre-back, who can also cover the right side of defence. Kounde, 27, certainly fits the bill as prior to joining Barcelona, he played in central defence for Sevilla and moved to full-back after signing for the Catalan giants, which is a position he also plays for the national team.

Kounde is said to be a cheaper alternative to Konsa, who has been valued at £60million by the Europa League champions. The Frenchman has reported for pre-season training in Spain and played a key role in Barca's back-to-back title triumphs.

View 3 Images Jules Kounde is reportedly a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



£85m star open to Premier League move

Bayer Leverkusen star Christian Kofane revealed that he'd be open to joining the Premier League in the future. The 20-year-old impressed in his debut season with the Bundesliga club, with seven goals and nine assists in 44 games.

The striker came up against the Gunners last season in the Champions League round of 16 and showcased his potential in both legs despite his side coming up short. His agent Eric Depolo seemingly claimed that his performances led to the Gunners enquiring about his situation, but warned them that they'd have to part ways with £85m to get his client.

He told Daily Arsenal earlier this year: "Yes, Arsenal's interest is genuine. The manager [Mikel Arteta] likes him very much. I think it is too early to say [which club is leading the race].

‌



View 3 Images Christian Kofane has been linked with a move to Arsenal since last season (Image: Getty Images)

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes' position decided as Myles Lewis-Skelly sends Arsenal message - 5 talking points

Arsenal took on Como at the Emirates Stadium in their final pre-season match before the Community Shield vs Man City

View 4 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid talk of him leaving Arsenal this summer

Arsenal have concluded their pre-season campaign, with eyes now on the weekend's Community Shield against Manchester City - the two teams meet in Cardiff on Sunday.

‌



In the final game before that meeting, the Gunners took on Italian side Como at the Emirates Stadium, a match which saw Cesc Fabregas return to his former home. The game ended in a 1-1 draw, with Arsenal winning thanks to a penalty shootout.

‌



Arsenal took the lead just after the first-half drinks break. Myles Lewis-Skelly capitalised on a mistake from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez. His clearance eventually found its way to Gabriel Martinelli, who got the ball back to the midfielder and he made no mistake to put Arsenal 1-0 up.

‌



But the Gunners didn't go into half time leading with Como making the most of a counter-attack. The ball made its way to Martin Baturina, who cut in from the left and gave Kepa Arrizabalaga no chance with a great finish to make it 1-1.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That's how the score would remain, despite chances for both sides. That meant that penalties were needed to separate the two sides, with summer signing Christos Tzolis scoring the decisive spot kick.

‌



Mirror Football has taken a look at some of the biggest talking points from the game.

Myles Lewis-Skelly message

Like previous pre-season games, Lewis-Skelly was named in the starting XI, despite being linked with a move away from the Emirates in recent days.

The 19-year-old played in midfield just in front of the back four. He also got forward when given the chance, and was rewarded by scoring the opening goal.

‌



He capitalised on a mistake from the Como goalkeeper, to put Arsenal 1-0 up just after the first-half drinks break. His celebration saw him make a heart with his hands, which was a clear sign of where his head is at. He received a warm reception from the Emirates crowd when he was replaced in the second half.

Bruno Guimaraes role

Bruno Guimaraes completed a £75 million move to Arsenal from Newcastle United last week. The Brazilian came on at half-time to make his debut for the club, much to the delight of those at the Emirates. He played a similar role to Declan Rice, playing just in front of Lewis-Skelly.

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes made his Arsenal debut vs Como (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



As expected, Guimaraes was always eager to get on the ball and make something happen. He also got back well and helped prevent a counter-attack, leading to chants of 'Bruno' from the home crowd. His introduction did allow Lewis-Skelly to get forward a bit more often.

Defensive issues

Despite not giving up many chances in the first-half, Arteta would have been frustrated to concede one of the few that Como had. While it was a great finish, there may have been an argument that more could have done to stop the ball getting to that position in the first place.

Defensive concerns are something that has dominated pre-season, with the team having conceded three goals in each of their previous two games against Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund. It's something that Arsenal will want to tighten up going into Sunday's Community Shield.

‌



If Arsenal give Man City similar chances, then they are likely to take them. Even if the game is seen as a 'glorified friendly', losing to title rivals ahead of the start of the season is not the ideal preparation for their Premier League opener.

Mikel Arteta decision

Marli Salmon was again given a chance to impress for Arsenal as he was named alongside Gabriel Magalhaes at the heart of defence. The injury to William Saliba has left Arteta short in the area.

View 4 Images Cesc Fabregas was back at the Emirates

‌



They have been linked with Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, but it seems the two teams are still far apart in their valuation. Salmon could provide a solution if Arsenal are unable to bring in a new defender in the transfer window, having impressed again against Como.

Despite being just 16, he earned praise for his composure, strength and willingness to step out of defence with the ball when needed.

Either way, a decision will have to be made over his short-term future. But it will be a bit of a waiting game for Arsenal.

‌



Players have to be on a professional contract to go out on loan, and they can't sign that contract until they are 17 years old. Salmon doesn't turn 17 until August 29, meaning that there will be just a few days for Arsenal to sort out a loan deal if they decide to send him out for valuable game time.

View 4 Images Marli Salmon staked his case for more involvement

It will be less complicated for Theo Julienne, who made his first pre-season appearance by starting at left-back. The 18-year-old didn’t look out of place, but a loan deal and regular game time this season may benefit him.

‌



Ethan Nwaneri chance

Ethan Nwaneri is another player who may have been playing for a place in the starting XI for the season opener against Coventry City in under two weeks.

Competition for places means that in the number 10 role Nwaneri has Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard vying for the same spot.

Article continues below

With Declan Rice still not back after the World Cup, Nwaneri was given the chance to impress in a slightly deeper role. Lewis-Skelly sitting allowed him to go forward and help Eze in the number 10 role; there was then more of an interchange when Fabio Vieira was introduced after half an hour.

He caught the eye in the opening stages, often playing a big role in the high press, which led to some early chances. He did, however, fade as the half went on and was replaced by Guimaraes at halftime.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
