World.title: How North Korea has profited from its support for Russia
World.content:
Exceptionally high revenues, particularly from war aid for Russia, are consolidating the power of North Korea's autocratic leader. A small number of people in the country are benefiting from an economic boom.

For years, satellite images of North Korea at night showed only a few small patches of light. Electricity shortages meant that even cities remained dark. In the six years since April 2020, however, the illuminated area in the center of Pyongyang has tripled in size.

The information portal NK News sees the increased illumination of the urban area as evidence that the regime has prioritized the supply of electricity to new streets and houses in the center to showcase its achievements.

At the last party congress in 2021, Kim Jong Un, North Korea's leader, announced that he would build 50,000 new apartments in the capital. And he did embark on the plan: in the new neighborhood of Hwasong, for example, with the construction of two 40-story apartment blocks shaped like Hwasong intercontinental ballistic missiles.

Why North Korea is now Europe's problem To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The new high-rise districts are not the only sign of North Korea's improved prosperity. People who have been visiting Pyongyang for a long time report that the city now appears more modern.

There are many imported cars, including electric cars from China, smartphone apps with QR codes to make payments or to call taxis, and department stores that stock Western fashion brands and cosmetics.

Pyongyang has transformed into a modern city thanks to North Korea's deals with Russia and China Image: Jon Chol Jin/AP Photo/picture alliance

The regime has completed construction in Pyongyang of the biggest hospital in the country and a hothouse the size of New York's Central Park. In June 2025, Kim officially opened the five-kilometer-long (3.3 miles) beach resort of Wonsan-Kalma on the east coast, with space for 20,000 guests.

In June, the Wall Street Journal described North Korea as the "world's most unlikely growth story."

North Korea's lucrative war deals with Russia

The dictatorship is presumably able to finance this sudden upturn thanks to the substantial income from its involvement in Russia's war against Ukraine.

According to a report by the South Korean Institute for National Security Strategy (INSS) in March, North Korea earns between $7.7 billion and $14.4 billion (€6.7 billion and €12.5 billion) from the sale of munitions to Moscow and the deployment of troops. Bloomberg Economics recently estimated that between 2022 and 2025, North Korea earned more than $14 billion by providing military support for Russia.

North Korea expands its role in Russia's war against Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Furthermore, it brought in another $8 billion through trade with China, the provision of North Korean workers to other countries, export business and online criminality. The hacking of the ByBit platform in February 2025 was one of the world's biggest cryptocurrency heists. Suspected North Korean hackers made off with $1.5 billion worth of Ethereum, a network with its own virtual currency. In comparison: the previous year, North Korea's entire GDP was $27 billion.

North Korea's involvement in Russia's war effort

It is unclear whether it was Russia or North Korea who first had the idea of using the impoverished country's massive stockpiles of munitions in Russia's war against Ukraine.

Kyiv estimates that in 2024 and 2025, North Korea supplied half the munitions Russia used at the front, as well as self-propelled guns, multiple rocket launchers and ballistic missiles. Ukraine says North Korea is currently planning to transfer a missile unit to Russia to fight against Ukraine, consisting of 90 soldiers, six launch pads and up to 120 missiles.

Between 16,000 and 22,000 North Korean soldiers are already helping Russia to drive Ukraine out of the border province of Kursk and clear the area of mines afterward. According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Kim now intends to station a further 30,000 to 50,000 soldiers in Russia.

Kim hails troops returning from Russia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The business is a lucrative one: The INSS report says that, every month, Kim receives $2,800 per North Korean soldier, $3,000 for an officer and $6,000 to $10,000 for every soldier killed in action.

As in Soviet times, the reciprocal arrangement is conducted primarily through exchange transactions. In exchange for munitions, arms and soldiers, Russia supplies North Korea with crude oil and oil products, grain and military goods from anti-aircraft systems to the technologies for building drones, missiles and submarines.

North Korea's new global stage

Kim's new role as Russia's supporter has given him greater political importance and military power, as demonstrated by the launch of two 5,000-ton destroyers. In all 15 of the years he has been in power, the autocratic leader has never had this much influence, or this much money.

North Korea gains critical intel by aiding Russia in Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It's an astonishing turnaround. Kim noticeably lost weight during the COVID-19 pandemic, and at the Workers' Party congress in 202,1 he shed tears as he admitted that the national economic development strategy had fallen "far short in almost all sectors."

At the next party congress five years later, with seven rows of artillery pieces lined up outside the building, Kim crowed, "Everything has fundamentally changed."

The partnership with Russia has allowed North Korea to shed its status as a pariah of world politics and overcome its isolation. In June 2024, the Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Kim in Pyongyang. Chinese leader Xi Jinping came in June of this year, three months after the Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko. In September 2025, Kim was in attendance at the celebrations in Beijing, alongside Xi and Putin, to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II.

Profits not reaching North Koreans

However, observers say this economic upswing is not benefiting the majority of the population.

Many households already in a precarious situation and without access to foreign currency have been hit hard by rising food prices and the devaluation of the won, the national currency. In many families, the women, too, must now go out to work in order to maintain living standards.

In the spring of 2024, Kim promoted a "20x10" development program for regions beyond the well-supplied capital Pyongyang. Presumably, he intends to finance this with the new additional revenue. The plan foresees that modern factories will be built in 20 cities or regions annually, creating 200 regional industrial projects over 10 years.

But according to Andrei Lankov, a professor and North Korea expert at Kookmin University in Seoul, the majority of the 20x10 projects fail.

"This is because not only do the factories have no infrastructure, they also do not take into account the mechanisms for supplying electricity, equipment, and raw materials," he said.

The factories are operated according to the principles of a planned economy, which is unsuited to small and medium-sized businesses.

"Unlike the economic growth that took place in North Korea in the mid-2010s, the current growth was based not on internal economic reforms, but only on international good fortune," Lankov said.

World.title: Brazil orders Discord to halt livestreaming after teen death
World.content:
Brazil has ordered Discord to suspend livestreaming as authorities scrutinize how the platform protects young users. The move follows a case described a "real-life horror show" that has triggered national outrage.

Brazil's data protection authority on Wednesday ordered the online messaging platform Discord to suspend its livestreaming feature in the country within three business days.

Officials cited failures to protect children and teenagers from content promoting violence, self-harm and suicide.

Why has Brazil ordered Discord to suspend livestreaming?

The National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) issued the measure after the death of a 13-year-old girl who investigators say was encouraged to harm herself and take her own life during a livestream on the platform.

"Live streams have been repeatedly used to facilitate violence, harassment, and the incitement of self-harm and suicide," said the ANPD.

It cited "robust evidence that the company failed to adopt reasonable measures" to protect children and teenagers from such content.

The regulator said Discord's "Go Live" feature would remain suspended until the company could demonstrate that effective technical, security and governance safeguards for minors were in place.

The ANPD said Discord lacked real-time access to livestream content, limiting its ability to automatically detect violations and leaving it reliant on user reports and other systems the regulator considers inadequate.

How to ensure children’s safety while gaming To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Discord has 10 business days to appeal the decision. It could face fines of up to 50 million reais ($9.7 million, €8.4 million) per violation if irregularities are confirmed.

What happened to the 13-year-old girl on Discord?

Police said the 13-year-old girl was encouraged during a roughly 45-minute livestream in July to harm herself and then die by suicide.

Authorities say members of an online group first encouraged her to carry out escalating violent "challenges," including harming an animal, before challenging her to broadcast her own suicide on Discord.

Police say the group deliberately sought out emotionally vulnerable children and teenagers.

Five teenagers and one adult were detained in connection with the case. Police said another girl who was allegedly preparing to take her own life during a livestream was also rescued during the investigation.

What has been the wider reaction in Brazil?

Brazil's Justice Ministry and police have criticized Discord's moderation and age-control systems. One official said one person involved in the case had been able to register an age of 148 using the platform's self-declaration system.

Brazilian first lady Rosangela "Janja" da Silva last week called for Discord to be completely blocked in the country following the teenager's death.

Discord representatives met Brazilian authorities on Friday and later submitted a plan aimed at strengthening protections for users under 18.

Brazil has tightened rules governing children's use of online platforms, including requirements on age verification and parental links for younger users.

*Editor's note: If you are suffering from serious emotional strain or suicidal thoughts, do not hesitate to seek professional help. You can find information on where to find such help, no matter where you live in the world, at this website: https://www.befrienders.org/

World.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
World.content:
A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

Eurovision Song Contest organizers announced rule changes that would prevent countries involved in an armed conflict from hosting the event.

Israel and Ukraine are among the countries the rule could affect, with both having enjoyed recent success in the competition.

What did the Eurovision organizers say?

Eurovision is typically staged by the broadcaster from the country that won the previous edition as part of a co-production involving members of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU).

Under the new rules, "the winning broadcaster will automatically be ineligible to host the Contest if an armed conflict, a sensitive geopolitical situation, or any other situation materially affects the security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region," the EBU said.

Canada to join 2027 Eurovision Song Contest To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The EBU may commission an independent security assessment if necessary. If the winning broadcaster is deemed unable to stage the contest, another broadcaster will be selected.

Why is the Eurovision changing the rules?

The EBU did not name any particular country as the reason, but Israel finished second at Eurovision in both 2025 and 2026.

Five countries — Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Iceland — boycotted the 2026 contest in Vienna, saying they could not participate alongside Israel because of the war in Gaza. Israel is currently involved in the war in Iran.

The new rule formalizes a challenge Eurovision has faced before.

Ukraine hosted the contest in 2017 despite fighting in the east of the country, but after winning Eurovision in 2022 it was unable to stage the following year's event because of Russia's full-scale invasion.

Liverpool instead hosted Eurovision 2023 in the United Kingdom on Ukraine's behalf.

Russia has been excluded from Eurovision since 2022, when the EBU banned it following its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

What else is changing about the Eurovision?

Under the new rules, the EBU is raising the minimum age for performers from 16 to 18 to reduce pressure on young artists.

Lead vocals must also be performed live and cannot be supported by pre-recorded voices.

Russia launches Eurovision rival music contest after ban To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The EBU said the clarification was intended to protect the integrity of performances and ensure audiences hear the lead singer live.

Eurovision director Martin Green said the contest's rules were reviewed each year to keep the competition fair and transparent.

Next year's contest will be held in Bulgaria following Bulgarian pop singer Dara's victory in Eurovision 2026 in Vienna with "Bangaranga."

World.title: El turismo, la fábrica de oportunidades de España
World.content:
Con cerca de 700.000 empresas y un récord de visitantes en el horizonte, el sector de los viajes, el alojamiento y el ocio premia a los emprendedores que se especializan en un nicho del mercado, buscan soluciones digitales o convierten la sostenibilidad en una ventaja competitiva

Si hay una industria proclive al emprendimiento ahora mismo en España, esa es la del turismo. Este boyante sector, uno de los principales motores económicos nacionales, no para de batir sus propias cifras. Este año se prevé que se acerque a los 100 millones de visitantes —después de alcanzar los 96,8 millones en 2025—, algo nunca visto en el segundo país más visitado del mundo, solo por detrás de Francia. Y ese volumen inédito, explica David Hernández, fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea, genera oportunidades de negocio en toda la cadena de valor: desde los alojamientos a la restauración, el ocio y el transporte.

Triunfar en el sector, asegura Asier Baquero, director del máster en Innovación en Turismo de la Universidad Internacional de La Rioja (UNIR), requiere, no obstante, de estrategia. “Hoy no basta con montar un hotel y esperar a que lleguen los huéspedes; el crecimiento también ha multiplicado la competitividad, por lo que resulta esencial diferenciarse para destacar”, explica el experto. Algo que se consigue a través de la adopción de soluciones innovadoras, de la especialización o de la atención a la creciente sensibilidad de los visitantes por la sostenibilidad.

Consejo de empresario Para emprender hay que ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya, te puedes llevar sorpresas David Hernández, Fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea

Digitalización para abrirse camino en el mercado

Las soluciones digitales se han convertido en una palanca de diferenciación en el sector del turismo. Hoy la mayoría de las empresas de éxito nacen en el ecosistema de start-ups para ofrecer soluciones directamente al consumidor. Es el caso de la barcelonesa ByHours, que comercializa habitaciones por horas en hoteles de todo el mundo, o el de la madrileña Civitatis, que ha revolucionado el mercado de las actividades turísticas en español al programar visitas guiadas y excursiones por ciudades de Europa, Latinoamérica, Estados Unidos y Asia. “Ambas han identificado una necesidad del turista y han aportado una solución digital que, además, se puede exportar a cualquier parte del globo”, puntualiza Baquero, que da una pista de por dónde puede ir el emprendimiento: “El objetivo de España ya no es atraer más a turistas, sino gestionar de manera más eficiente la estancia de los que visitan el país”.

Otras empresas de ese ecosistema digital, explica Baquero, se crean con el objetivo de brindar soluciones a las grandes agencias de viajes o a las cadenas hoteleras. “Así sucede con los asistentes de inteligencia artificial para centralitas que gestionan las llamadas de los hoteles y las conectan con las reservas, algo que les permite ahorrar muchos recursos”, explica Baquero.

Jugar la baza de la especialización y la sostenibilidad

Encontrar una solución para un grupo concreto de consumidores es otra de las maneras de empezar con buen pie en el sector. Baquero afirma que hoy los hoteles o las agencias de viaje necesitan un apellido: “Un hotel burbuja, una agencia de viajes de lujo o para el segmento LGTBIQ+...”, ejemplifica el experto. Esta es una de las razones que explica el éxito de Nomading Camp, una empresa especializada en alojamientos de lujo en entornos naturales, con propuestas como suites y habitaciones burbuja en cinco destinos, desde los Pirineos hasta la sierra malagueña de Ronda. Lo justifica su fundador, Miquel Vila: “En nuestro caso, la experiencia es muy importante. No ofrecemos solo una cama, sino una noche en pleno bosque con todas las comodidades. La propia habitación es la experiencia. Nuestros clientes no nos escogen porque quieren ir a un destino y necesitan un sitio para dormir, sino que primero escogen nuestra experiencia y luego se desplazan hasta donde van a vivirla”, describe el empresario.

Emprender en el turismo tiene una dificultad añadida frente a otros sectores: no se venden productos, sino experiencias. Un fabricante puede controlar casi todas las características de lo que produce, pero una empresa turística depende de multitud de factores que determinan cómo recordará el cliente su viaje: la atención, el clima, las expectativas del viajero, la coordinación entre distintos servicios... Por eso, el éxito no consiste solo en ofrecer un buen servicio, sino en conseguir que el visitante viva una experiencia que merezca la pena recomendar, defiende Hernández, de Pangea. “Vendemos viajes a destinos cercanos, pero también a 10.000 kilómetros de distancia, con 20 proveedores, por lo que hay una alta probabilidad de que algo salga mal”, destaca.

Consejo de empresario Sigue tu propio camino sin fijarte en el camino de otros emprendedores Miquel Vila, fundador de los alojamientos de lujo en plena naturaleza Nomading Camp

La sostenibilidad gana cada vez más peso como ventaja en esta industria, asegura Baquero. Porque no solo responde a una creciente demanda de los viajeros, sino que también contribuye a reducir costes, acceder a financiación y cumplir la normativa. Por eso cada vez más compañías deciden que su propuesta de valor esté claramente ligada a la sostenibilidad, la economía circular o la conservación del entorno. La catalana Turismo Vivencial se ha hecho un hueco en el mercado ofreciendo consultoría sobre ecoturismo, el turismo respetuoso con el medio ambiente, y organiza actividades que contribuyen a conservar el patrimonio natural y cultural, así como generar beneficios a las comunidades locales. Cada vez son más comunes las compañías que ayudan a negocios del sector a medir su impacto ambiental, como la valenciana Bioscore Sustainability y la madrileña GreeMKO, que no es exclusiva del sector turístico, pero desarrolla programas para la gestión ambiental y el cálculo automatizado de la huella de carbono de hoteles.

Lecciones de los emprendedores

David Hernández y Miquel Vila, que protagonizan el último capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen , de Banco Sabadell, comparten algunas de las lecciones que han aprendido después de emprender y que pueden ser de utilidad para los empresarios de hoy y mañana. Vila, de Nomading Camp, asegura que, con el tiempo y la distancia, le hubiera gustado compararse menos con otros emprendedores y haber hecho caso a su instinto más frecuentemente: “Merece la pena seguir tu propio camino. Por ejemplo, si tus competidores están haciendo rondas de inversión y tú sientes que no necesitas una nueva, no la hagas; tu gran meta ha de ser que tu negocio funcione, no la ronda en sí misma”. Hernández, de Pangea, señala una actitud como clave a la hora de enfrentarse a cualquier decisión: “No hay que ser demasiado optimista. Me explico: creo que para ser emprendedor es imprescindible ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya luego te puedes llevar sorpresas”.

World.title: La redefinición de los ligues de verano: no tienen por qué acabar en relación y las ‘apps’ se adaptan a las nuevas realidades
World.content:
Con los días contados y un montón de fantasías por realizar, la seducción es un reto en las semanas estivales e incluso una presión para muchos. Mientras el ‘dating’ turístico vive su agosto, los expertos recuerdan que tenemos el resto del año para ligar

En estilos de vida cada vez más predecibles, monótonos y alienantes, las vacaciones se convierten en ese permiso penitenciario que hay que exprimir al máximo. Sexualmente hablando, el verano aumenta el deseo (aunque ya hay teorías que dicen lo contrario, por las altas temperaturas) y los días libres, los viajes y las noches de fiesta favorecen las posibilidades de encuentros eróticos. El problema surge cuando esa posibilidad, explotada por el cine en tantas películas —Vacaciones en Roma (1953), El diario de Noa (2004), Antes del amanecer (1995) o Locuras de verano (1955), entre otras—, se convierte en un deber.

El pasado año, la web de viajes baratos Holidayguru llevó a cabo una encuesta entre 2.000 españoles para averiguar cómo se relacionan los viajeros con el amor, el sexo y las aplicaciones de citas durante el verano. El 65% reconocía haber ligado alguna vez durante sus vacaciones, aunque el entusiasmo parecía enfriarse al mirar al futuro: en 2025, solo un 27% planeaba ligar en verano, mientras que un contundente 73% aseguraba que no lo tenía entre sus planes. En otra encuesta realizada este año a 169 mujeres solteras y heterosexuales en España, realizada por la marca de juguetería erótica y bienestar sexual femenino Womanizer, casi la mitad (46,5%) asegura que ligar es más difícil que hace unos años. Con un 46,8% de mujeres que reconocen no confiar en encontrar pareja en este momento, los resultados dibujan un panorama de creciente incertidumbre para las relaciones.

Los expertos ya hablan de la dating app fatigue (fatiga de las aplicaciones de citas). Cada vez más usuarios dicen sentirse cansados del swipe (arrastrar el dedo para pasar a un nuevo perfil). Aun así, muchas personas siguen registrándose o permaneciendo en este tipo de portales. No tanto para encontrar a alguien, ni siquiera para quedar, sino como distracción, sobre todo entre mujeres. Alicia, madrileña de 31 años, es usuaria de Tinder desde el verano pasado. “Me descargué la aplicación en un viaje que hice con otras amigas, más de broma que otra cosa. No ligué con nadie, pero ver los perfiles, las descripciones, las fotos y los comentarios era parte de la diversión”. En esta línea, una amiga alemana me ha metido en un chat sobre las luces y sombras de las apps de citas, que algunos ya no utilizan para ligar, sino para debatir sobre el proceso, puesto que su fin primigenio (encontrar pareja o echar una cala al aire) se empieza a vislumbrar ya como un espejismo.

Por su parte, las celestinas digitales, conocedoras de este problema, tratan de introducir cambios para seguir existiendo. Bumble, el portal para ligar que destaca por exigir que, en los contactos heterosexuales, sean las mujeres las únicas que puedan dar el primer paso —enviando el mensaje inicial tras el necesario match—, ha incorporado algunos cambios tras un reciente estudio que ha revelado las siguientes conclusiones: cada vez más usuarios en España afrontan el dating con un mayor grado de reflexión y autoconocimiento. En lugar de atribuir las malas experiencias a la mala suerte o a las personas con las que han salido, un 64% afirma haber reflexionado sobre su propio comportamiento en las citas durante el último año y un destacado 82% prefiere aprender de las relaciones que no funcionaron antes que repetir los mismos errores. Incluso la idea de un ligue de verano puede redefinirse.

Las vacaciones son una época en la que muchas personas están más abiertas a conocer gente. Klaus Vedfelt (Getty Images)

Según Chantelle Otten, experta en relaciones de Bumble, “las vacaciones son una época en la que muchas personas están más abiertas a conocer gente y vivir interacciones más espontáneas. Sin embargo, una conexión de verano no tiene por qué definirse únicamente por si termina convirtiéndose o no en una relación a largo plazo”. Y añade: “Estamos viendo una evolución en la manera en que las personas entienden este tipo de encuentros. Cada vez más usuarios, especialmente muchas mujeres, definen por sí mismos qué significa tener una experiencia positiva. Una conexión puede ser valiosa tanto si continúa después del verano como si simplemente representa una experiencia divertida, auténtica o que ayuda a ganar confianza. Más que centrarse en la idea de relaciones pasajeras, lo importante es que las personas sientan la libertad de relacionarse de la forma que mejor encaje con ellas, sin asumir que todas las conexiones deben seguir el mismo camino para tener significado”.

Cuando el ligue está (casi) garantizado

Mientras muchas apps luchan por sobrevivir introduciendo cambios, otras se especializan en el fast and furious del ligue veraniego. Algunas incluso aprovechan los trayectos para ir ahorrando tiempo. Es el caso de Wingle, una aplicación gratuita que permite conectar, charlar y conocer a otros pasajeros del mismo vuelo sin necesidad de pagar por internet a bordo.

Algunas aplicaciones de citas se han adaptado al turismo de verano, aprovechando incluso los trayectos entre destinos. Kathrin Ziegler (Getty Images)

Pero, ¿por qué esperar a llegar al aeropuerto si uno puede ligar en las vacaciones antes incluso de que estas hayan comenzado? Ligar antes de viajar es ya una tendencia consolidada. La función Passport de Tinder, que permite cambiar la ubicación virtual a cualquier ciudad del mundo para buscar, hacer match y chatear con personas antes de ir a otro país, sigue creciendo como herramienta para preparar encuentros antes de llegar al destino. En el resumen anual de Tinder de 2024 se hablaba de una media de 145.000 usos diarios de Passport y de un fuerte incremento de su utilización en grandes destinos turísticos. De hecho, las ciudades con gran afluencia de visitantes en verano (Palma, Ibiza, Barcelona, Lisboa, Mikonos, Roma…) son también donde más se abren este tipo de funciones, para quienes buscan “algo para el verano”, “un guía local”, un “compañero de viaje” o “alguien que conozca los mejores restaurantes”, a menudo eufemismos para designar el rollete de las vacaciones.

Así que, mientras el ligue digital vive sus horas bajas, el dating turístico crece gracias a las nuevas fórmulas para interactuar con los nativos, antes incluso de sacar el billete de avión. De hecho, un sondeo británico de 2025 reveló que el 60% de los solteros vuelve a activar las aplicaciones de citas cuando va al extranjero, un 18% reconoce que el potencial para ligar influye en la elección de su lugar de vacaciones y un 36% considera los romances de verano como algo puramente temporal y sin demasiadas repercusiones en sus vidas.

En el universo analógico, al que cada vez más gente vuelve escarmentada del flirteo digital, los viajes para solteros ganan adeptos. Asegurando los ingredientes básicos: gente con ganas de conectar, vacaciones y viajes, ¿qué puede salir mal? Tuymilmas es una empresa especializada en escapadas para singles, sobre todo por España, aunque también hacen rutas internacionales. “Entre el 60 y el 65% de nuestros clientes son mujeres entre 40 y 55 años”, apunta Beatriz Carrillo, CEO de la empresa. “La gente que busca ligar, ya sea para encontrar pareja o para echar una cana al aire, y quiere cogerse unos días de vacaciones aúna estos dos propósitos. Es muy fácil intimar porque vas en grupo y las actividades se hacen conjuntamente. La mayoría de los destinos son nacionales, lo que hace que el ritmo del viaje sea más lento y se disponga de más tiempo libre. Tenemos ya algunas parejas que se han casado y que se conocieron en nuestros viajes; aunque a la mayoría le cuesta reconocer que nos eligen para ligar. La excusa es que no les apetece viajar solos”, reconoce Carrillo.

Algunos estudios apuntan a que el 60% de los solteros vuelve a activar las aplicaciones de citas cuando viaja al extranjero. Kathrin Ziegler (Getty Images)

Lo cierto es que la tecnología, capaz de conectarnos con cualquiera que tenga wifi, aunque sea al otro lado del mundo, ha acabado con la magia de los amores de verano, intensos por obra y gracia de su ineludible fecha de caducidad. “Los ligues de vacaciones tenían mucho morbo y libertad porque ambas partes sabían que tenían un final”, cuenta el Raúl González Castellanos, también psicopedagogo y terapeuta de pareja del gabinete de apoyo terapéutico A la Par, en Madrid. “Yo creo que esa magia se ha ido perdiendo porque ahora la gente permanece en contacto por WhatsApp o espía al otro en las redes sociales. Hay, además, una presión de pasarlo bien en las vacaciones, de ser feliz, y eso incluye ligar para mucha gente. Así, el amor de verano se llena de prisa, de ansiedad, de miedo al fracaso, de vergüenza por volver sin una historia que contar a los amigos”.

En opinión de González, “hay que experimentar el verano y las naturales ganas de ligar de manera menos ansiosa. Vivir lo que nos apetece realmente, y no lo que se supone que debemos vivir. Tiene que quedarnos claro que el verano no es un examen de vida y que se puede ligar todo el año”. Y lanza un consejo: “Hay también que respetar los sentimientos ajenos, ser sinceros y no infundir falsas esperanzas para no herir a nadie. Y no está de más tener en cuenta que las personas más sensibles o vulnerables, que atraviesan un estado emocional más bajo o alterado, deberían pensarse dos veces si van a ser capaces de pasar página sin mayores consecuencias ni dramas; o si, por el contrario, el ligue de verano va a aumentar su sufrimiento o ansiedad”.

World.title: La expulsión masiva de afganos de Pakistán desborda la frontera y deja a miles de niñas sin escolarizar de un día para otro
World.content:
Un grupo de niños en Torkham, en la frontera entre Pakistán y Afganistán el pasado junio, por donde cruzan a diario miles de afganos en cumplimiento del plan de repatriación impulsado por el Gobierno pakistaní.

Más de 2,6 millones de ciudadanos de Afganistán han salido del país vecino desde 2023 como consecuencia de un estricto plan de repatriación aplicado por el Gobierno de Islamabad

Durante 27 años, Ahmad Khan, de origen afgano, vivió en Pakistán. En la ciudad de Sialkot, en el norte, regentaba una pequeña zapatería, sus niños iban a la escuela local y su hijo mayor trabajaba en un puesto de shawarma muy cerca de casa. En la mezquita del barrio, todo el mundo lo conocía. Pero llegó la campaña de represión de Pakistán contra los migrantes afganos y fue expulsado, junto con su mujer, seis hijos y dos hijas, el pasado noviembre.

Las perspectivas en Afganistán, donde los talibanes han vuelto al poder desde que las fuerzas estadounidenses se retiraran en 2021, son muy sombrías para los deportados y en particular para las mujeres, sometidas a un apartheid de género, según la ONU. “La situación en Afganistán es muy mala”, afirma Khan por teléfono desde ese país. “No hay trabajo ni un sistema educativo adecuado, especialmente para las niñas a partir de los 12 años”. Bajo el régimen talibán, las mujeres no tienen acceso a la educación secundaria . Una niña matriculada en una clase una semana en Pakistán puede encontrarse al otro lado de la frontera la siguiente, sin colegio al que acudir.

Como Khan, más de 2,6 millones de afganos han retornado al país desde 2023, como consecuencia de un estricto plan de repatriación aplicado por el Gobierno pakistaní. De acuerdo con la Agencia de la ONU para los Refugiados (Acnur), solo entre el 1 de enero y el 1 de agosto de 2026, han regresado más de 723.000 personas. Muchos de los deportados son afganos nacidos en Pakistán que nunca han puesto un pie en Afganistán. Hablan urdu, no dari ni pastún. Las calles, las escuelas y los campos de juego que conocen son pakistaníes.

El aumento de las deportaciones ha convertido la frontera en un escenario de miseria, donde las familias afganas sufren escasez de alimentos y agua en medio de un calor abrasador y la falta de refugio, todo ello mientras se enfrentan a la incertidumbre de lo que les depara el futuro.

Khan se vio además obligado a cruzar de vuelta por Torkham, el paso fronterizo más transitado que une Pakistán y Afganistán y por donde pasan hasta entre 4.000 y 6.000 personas al día. Su familia se quedó atrapada durante tres o cuatro días debido a la abrumadora congestión, recuerda. Desde marzo, la situación en Torkham no ha hecho más que empeorar. Los afganos que regresan se han enfrentado a cierres fronterizos, colapsos en los servicios migratorios, campamentos de tránsito con carencias y hasta desastres climáticos. A mediados de julio, por ejemplo, el paso fronterizo quedó interrumpido por las crecidas de agua repentinas que afectaron a la región. Tres refugiados afganos murieron y otros nueve resultaron heridos.

La implacable oleada de deportaciones es el resultado del Plan de Repatriación de Extranjeros Ilegales que Pakistán puso en marcha en 2023 para expulsar a todos los ciudadanos extranjeros que considera que residen en el país de forma ilegal. A partir de ese año, se intensificaron las redadas, se colocaron avisos en los barrios afganos y los rumores de deportación se extendieron por las estrechas calles y los concurridos mercados. Algunas familias se marcharon discretamente tras las redadas nocturnas. Otras esperaron, con la esperanza de que la presión cediera. Pero, en 2025, la campaña se reforzó y las perspectivas para los afganos migrantes y refugiados empeoraron. La capacidad de tramitación de expulsiones no ha podido seguir el ritmo, provocando la congestión de la frontera.

Una crisis que se mide en millones

Torkham estuvo prácticamente cerrad a entre octubre y marzo, cuando los enfrentamientos fronterizos con Afganistán se intensificaron hasta dar lugar a la Operación Ghazab lil Haq , una campaña militar pakistaní lanzada en febrero contra los talibanes y los militantes vinculados al grupo.

El paso fronterizo reabrió para los repatriados afganos a finales de marzo bajo estrictas medidas de seguridad, con toques de queda en los alrededores de la terminal y los trámites migratorios canalizados exclusivamente a través de Hamza Baba, un punto de tránsito a pocos kilómetros de Torkham. Tras la reapertura, los flujos de personas se dispararon en un 727% en menos de una semana, según datos de Acnur. El 95% de los repatriados indocumentados aseguraron que se habían marchado por miedo a ser detenidos.

Para quienes se encuentran en la frontera, las condiciones se están deteriorando rápidamente. Bagzari Hamid Ullah, una mujer de 34 años procedente de Sialkot y madre de cuatro hijos, esperó en el paso fronterizo de Torkham durante seis días sin comida ni refugio. Su marido había sido detenido durante una redada en Punyab en marzo y se vieron obligados a irse ese mismo mes.

“Era una niña, probablemente de seis o siete años, cuando llegamos a Pakistán. Me casé aquí. Formé mi hogar aquí. Mis hijos nacieron aquí”, cuenta a EL PAÍS. “La tumba de mi padre está aquí. Por eso, al marcharme de Pakistán, siento que he dejado atrás la parte más preciada de mí misma”.

Los camiones que transportan a refugiados afganos cruzan el paso fronterizo de Torkham, entre Pakistán y Afganistán. Aqsa Younis

Algunas familias explican que la espera se puede prolongar hasta por dos semanas. En marzo, un incendio en el bazar de Torkham destruyó decenas de tiendas, lo que redujo aún más los servicios disponibles para las personas varadas.

La de Afganistán es una de las crisis de desplazamiento más prolongadas del mundo. Las agencias internacionales estiman que más de 10 millones de afganos viven desplazados en el exterior como consecuencia de décadas de guerra y conflictos internos.

Irán y Pakistán, los dos países en los que viven más afganos exiliados, han intensificado sus campañas de deportación. Según la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM), más de seis millones de afganos han regresado desde estos dos países desde septiembre de 2023. Esto ha implicado un aumento súbito de la población del 10% en Afganistán.

Un nuevo desarraigo

Las autoridades pakistaníes afirman que la política responde a razones de seguridad nacional, control de la inmigración y soberanía. Apuntan a la migración irregular y al extremismo transfronterizo, y sostienen que la ley debe aplicarse por igual a todos. Sin embargo, sobre el terreno se ha percibido como el desarraigo de toda una población. Familias que construyeron sus vidas durante décadas en Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar y Sialkot fueron reclasificadas como extranjeras casi de la noche a la mañana. Se cerraron negocios, se retiraron puestos de trabajo y los propietarios se negaron a renovar los contratos de alquiler. Una familia tras otra comenzó a hacer las maletas para ir a un país que muchos de ellos nunca habían visto.

Los expertos de la ONU afirman que entre las personas obligadas a regresar se encuentran cientos de miles de menores, tanto de familias con documentación como sin ella. Solo en 2025, el 60% de los retornados eran menores de edad.

Abiha Nawaz, psicóloga consultora del Hospital Al Sheikh de Sialkot, afirma que el daño causado a estos niños es profundo. “Este tipo de desplazamiento es extremadamente perjudicial, porque a los niños les resulta difícil asimilar lo que se les ha arrebatado”, explica. El daño, añade, comienza con la pérdida del único hogar que han conocido. “La incertidumbre genera miedo y ansiedad en los niños, porque consideran que Pakistán es su hogar”, afirma Nawaz.

Mis hijas nacieron aquí. Aquí tienen su colegio, sus clases y sus amigos. Están muy tristes, porque están dejando atrás su infancia Bagzari Hamid Ullah, mujer afgana

Para las niñas, advierte, la situación es aún más grave. “Mis hijas nacieron aquí. Aquí tienen su colegio, sus clases y sus amigos. Están muy tristes, porque están dejando atrás su infancia”, dice Ullah.

Bebés y niños enfermos

Los campamentos de tránsito en el lado afgano, como el de Omari, desempeñan un papel crucial. Se encargan de tramitar y controlar a los ciudadanos afganos que regresan a casa y de proporcionar ayuda humanitaria de emergencia. Pero también allí los funcionarios tienen dificultades para dar abasto e incluso se enfrentan a interrupciones debido a los recientes enfrentamientos transfronterizos y ataques aéreos, según explica Jawad Shinwari, que trabaja como voluntario en la frontera.

“Los niños se encuentran entre los más afectados”, afirma Shinwari. “Los bebés y los niños pequeños enferman y durante los aguaceros la gente se cubre con bolsas de plástico a falta de algo mejor”.

Muchos repatriados llegan a Afganistán con pocos o ningún recurso, tras haber vivido en Pakistán durante décadas. “No es posible empaquetar toda tu casa y mudarte a otro país”, señala Shinwari. “Los recursos en los campamentos también son limitados. Es frecuente ver escasez de alimentos, alojamiento y agua mientras la gente espera a que se tramiten sus expedientes”.

Los trabajadores humanitarios afirman que esto no ha hecho más que agravar la presión sobre las familias ya agotadas por el desplazamiento, y las organizaciones humanitarias sostienen que los retornos deben ir acompañados de garantías de derechos humanos.

“No tenemos ni hogar ni un alojamiento adecuado”, afirma Sumandar Khan, que viene desde Daska, en el norte de Pakistán y lleva más de una semana esperando cruzar. “Varios miembros de nuestra familia están enfermos y nos enfrentamos a graves dificultades económicas”. Al igual que muchos repatriados, espera que las autoridades concedan a su familia tierras y acceso a la asistencia sanitaria básica. En el lado afgano, el portavoz adjunto del Gobierno, Hamdullah Fitrat, afirmó en junio que habían asignado 42.614 parcelas residenciales a las familias repatriadas como parte de una iniciativa nacional de reintegración. Mientras, las proyecciones de la OIM apuntan a que casi 2,7 millones de personas saldrán entre abril y diciembre de 2026 en dirección al país de los talibanes.

World.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
World.content:
Vielha (Lleida). La gran baza de los pueblos seleccionados radica, sobre todo, en la posibilidad de tener que taparse para descansar, algo que se ha convertido en todo un lujo durante la canícula. Es un requisito que cumple Vielha, a la vera de los ríos Garona y Nere, con su casco histórico construido a la manera aranesa, a golpe de piedra, pizarra y madera. Sus mínimas descenderán hasta los 12ºC la noche del domingo; las máximas alcanzarán picos de 33ºC en las horas centrales del jueves y viernes, pero bajarán a los 24ºC (y con probabilidad de lluvias) el lunes, según la Aemet. La capital del Valle de Arán se presenta como un buen campamento base para conocer este territorio del Pirineo catalán, con sus 33 núcleos de población, sus algo más de 10.000 habitantes y sus iglesias románicas. Es recomendable acercarse a la cascada Saut deth Pish, probablemente la más bonita de la zona. Más información: visitvaldaran.com/descubre-la-val-daran/pueblos/vielha/.

World.title: Your takeaway habit is feeding Dutch inflation, says DNB
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch households are spending so much on takeaway meals that it is impacting national inflation, the Dutch central bank DNB has reported.

Delivery meals have nearly doubled as a share of the average shopping basket, from around 1.6% in 2015 to just over 3% today, DNB said on Thursday.

Prices have climbed fast. With more people spending, delivery firms have also passed on higher wage, energy and ingredient costs, and between 2020 and 2023 the category went from adding less than 0.1 percentage point to inflation to a full 0.35 point.

It has since eased back to 0.13 point – but only because prices stopped rising so fast, not because anyone is ordering less, DNB said.

The bank traces consumer habits back to the Covid pandemic, when locked-down households began using ordering apps much more, especially while working from home.

Dutch inflation has sat above the European Central Bank’s 2% target for years, driven mainly by rents and food prices. The pizza and sushi deliveries are now also hitting the figures.

World.title: Monument against violence in youth care system vandalized
World.content:
Just two months after it was unveiled, the national youth care monument (Nationaal Monument Jeugdzorg) commemorating violence against young people in the system was vandalised in Apeldoorn.

“This feels like a new attack,” Naomi van Aggelen told broadcaster NOS. She worked for years on the monument and was herself wrongly sent to live at a youth care institution when she was 12 years old.

“It is a very sad sight,” she said of the monument meant to acknowledge the suffering of young people in care homes. “Actually, [it’s] a denial of that recognition.”

Located in Apeldoorn’s Zuiderpark, the wings of the monument – titled De Erkenning (The Recognition) – were broken off and are now missing while scratches and dents are visible on what remains.

“Who does such a thing? We have no idea,” said Van Aggelen. “We don’t know where the wings are.”

The council has filed a police report and is said to be reviewing if additional security measures are needed.

The monument was commissioned after a 2019 report by De Winter Commission that found since WW2, some 20,000 children were the victims of violence in youth care. The organising foundation calls it a place of reparation, remembrance and “of vigilance: all current forms of violence must also stop.”

The future of the monument is still unclear. “I have no idea if we should leave the work for what it is,” said Van Aggelen. “Maybe we should glue it, then it symbolises another broken child in youth care.”

World.title: Barcelona legend Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach
World.content:
Xavi Hernández has been appointed head coach of the Netherlands men’s national team on a contract running to the 2030 World Cup, the Dutch football association KNVB has announced.

The 46-year-old Spaniard succeeds Ronald Koeman, who stepped down after the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup. His appointment ends a long and closely watched search, and comes as a surprise after several higher-profile names fell away.

Former Feyenoord and Liverpool coach Arne Slot, ex-Ajax and Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag and PSV’s Peter Bosz all ruled themselves out, while the KNVB passed over Jong Oranje coach Michael Reiziger and Louis van Gaal. On

Tuesday, Roberto Martínez was reportedly the front-runner, though the KNVB never held direct talks with him.

“A son of Dutch football”

Xavi becomes the first foreign coach of Oranje since the Austrian Ernst Happel, who led the side to the 1978 World Cup final.

“It is a great honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team,” he said in a statement released by the KNVB. “As someone who was developed at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from, among others, Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say I am, in a way, a son of Dutch football.”

As a player, Xavi is regarded as one of the best midfielders of his generation, winning four Champions League titles in more than 750 games for Barcelona and lifting the 2010 World Cup with Spain – beating the Netherlands in the final – as well as the European Championship in 2008 and 2012.

He started out as a coach at Al Sadd in Qatar, then took charge of Barcelona in 2021 – also succeeding Koeman – and won the Spanish league title in 2023, but made little impression in Europe before leaving in 2024.

Restoring tactics

The KNVB has handed Xavi an explicit task: restore the attacking, possession-based football long associated with the Dutch game, after a World Cup exit widely seen as a low point in style as much as result.

“As a coach, he has been shaped by years of working with top coaches who share a footballing vision that aligns very well with the way we want the Netherlands national team to play,” said the KNVB’s director Nigel de Jong. He pointed to “taking the initiative, playing dominant and attractive football, combined with the flexibility required in modern football at the highest level.”

Xavi said he shared that ambition. “The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that strongly appeals to me: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion and conviction,” he said. “The main objective is always to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy watching.”

He will be presented at the KNVB’s Zeist headquarters on August 25 and takes charge for the first time on September 24, at home to Germany in the Nations League.

World.title: NL breaks 1947 heat record with 31 tropical days in a year
World.content:
The Netherlands has recorded more tropical days in a single year than at any point since records began, after the temperature hit 31.5° in Maastricht on Tuesday.

It was the 31st day this year on which 30° or more – the threshold for a tropical day – was reached somewhere in the country, beating the record of 30 set in 1947.

Back then, the 30th tropical day did not arrive until September. This year the record fell in mid-August with weeks of potential summer heat still to come, and forecasters expect the tally to rise further.

The national weather service KNMI has linked the growing number of tropical days and back-to-back heatwaves to climate change.

The heat coincides with the second driest summer since measurements began in 1901 – only 1976 was drier – with the Rhine at its lowest in almost 80 years.

The public health institute RIVM has reactivated its national heat plan for the fourth time across the whole country from Wednesday, urging people to check on the elderly and young children and to keep homes cool.

Friday is forecast to be the hottest day, with highs of 33° to 37° and the chance of a fifth regional heatwave of the year, before cooler air moves in at the weekend.

World.title: Ukrainian soldier murdered by Soviets exhumed in Rotterdam
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The remains of a Ukrainian soldier who was murdered in Rotterdam by the Soviet secret services in 1938 are being repatriated for a military burial.

Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, the founder of a Ukrainian nationalist group, was killed by a bomb concealed in a box of chocolates as he walked home from a meeting with an undercover agent.

The Soviet spy had infiltrated the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and handed Konovalets the chocolates as a gift during a meeting at a hotel in Rotterdam on May 23, 1938.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky announced on his official website that the colonel’s remains had been exhumed at Crooswijk Cemetery in Rotterdam so that they could be sent back to Ukraine.

He will be temporarily reinterred at the National Military Memorial Cemetery, in preparation for a farewell ceremony will be held at the Ukrainan Greek Catholic cathedral in Kyiv.

The OUN was founded in 1929 in Vienna as a right-wing nationalist organisation that aimed to establish an independent, ethnically homogenous Ukrainian state.

It was influenced in its early days by Italian fascism and German Nazism, but as Germany’s defeat in the Second World War drew nearer, the OUN adopted a more democratic ideology.

World.title: ABN Amro profit climbs to €781m as fees, lending grow
World.content:
ABN Amro has booked net profit of €781 million in the second quarter, up 29% on the same period last year and ahead of analyst forecasts, the bank said on Wednesday.

Analysts had expected earnings of around €686 million. The result beat even the highest forecast in that consensus, and shares in the group rose more than 5% to a record high.

The bank, which is now around one-fifth owned by the Dutch state after reducing its stake following the 2008 financial crisis, is in the process of a reorganisation that will cut 5,200 jobs by 2028.

The state is close to recouping the full €21.7 billion cost of the 2008 nationalisation of the bank, following a share price rally that took the bank’s stock above €40 this week.

World.title: Limburg wildfire wiped out rare juniper shrubland
World.content:
Fewer than 100 of the roughly 4,000 juniper bushes that grew in the Boschhuizerbergen nature reserve near Venray have survived this month’s wildfire in northern Limburg, the foundation that manages the site says.

The reserve held the largest juniper shrubland in the southern Netherlands, according to Het Limburgs Landschap, with some bushes more than 130 years old. Junipers grow slowly and thrive in the reserve’s nutrient-poor, drifting-sand soil – conditions that have become rare in the region.

The fire, which broke out on August 3, destroyed around 100 hectares, including 20 to 30 hectares of protected Natura 2000 land where the junipers stood. More than a week on, crews were still pouring water on smouldering hotspots to stop them reigniting.

The shrubland might not be able to be re-established, as the soil has changed over the decades and young plants may struggle to take root. “It is questionable whether we will ever get such a beautiful shrubland here again. I am afraid I will not live to see it,” the foundation’s Loek Hendrikx told broadcaster NOS.

Het Limburgs Landschap, set up in 1931 to stop the reserve being cleared for farmland, has appealed for donations towards a recovery it says will take years.

World.title: Human rights groups sue US government over Hague court sanctions
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Four US human rights organisations have sued the Trump administration over its sanctions against the International Criminal Court in The Hague, arguing the measures are unconstitutional and should be struck down.

The American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch and the Open Society Institute filed the complaint in New York on Tuesday.

It challenges the executive order signed by US president Donald Trump in February 2025, which authorised sanctions on court officials and on anyone assisting its investigations.

Washington has since used it against the court’s former chief prosecutor and two of his deputies, eight of its judges, a UN human rights expert and three Palestinian rights organisations.

The four organisations say the measures have forced them to drop work such as representing war crimes victims and making legal submissions to the court, in breach of their rights to free speech, association and religion under the US constitution.

They also argue the order exceeds the president’s powers and rests on a declared national emergency that has no basis in fact, describing it as a “blatantly illegal attack on international justice”.

Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch, said governments should step up to protect the court and those seeking justice before it.

The case follows Washington’s announcement in July of a campaign to dismantle the court, which the Netherlands hosts and has a duty as host state to protect.

Federal courts in New York and Maine ruled in 2025 that the order breached free speech protections, blocking enforcement against the claimants in those cases.

The Polish government has appealed to Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, to reverse its decision to exclude Poland from its European roaming area. It says that Polish users, who will now face greater costs when travelling, should not be treated as “second-tier customers”. Starlink, which provides users with portable terminals that act as receivers for internet connections from its network of satellites, offers a “Roam” service that lets customers continue using their connection outside their home country without extra charges as long as they remain within their designated region. One region is Europe, in which Starlink has included 36 countries and territories. However, the firm makes clear that “Poland is not included in the Europe region”, meaning users registered in that country are not included in the Roam system. The company offered no explanation for Poland’s exclusion from the system. Some media reports have suggested that it is because terminals registered in Poland are used in Ukraine. However, Ukraine is itself not included in Starlink’s European “Roam” region. The company’s decision prompted an angry response from Polish government ministers. “I do not agree with a global technology company treating Poles worse than other Europeans,” wrote digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on X, the social media platform owned by Musk. “If Elon Musk’s SpaceX wants to operate in Poland, benefit from the Polish market, and earn from Polish customers, it must treat them fairly and on equal terms,” he added. “That is why I have appealed to SpaceX for the urgent restoration of equal terms for the company’s Polish customers.” Nie zgadzam się, żeby globalna firma technologiczna traktowała Polki i Polaków gorzej niż innych Europejczyków. World.title: Negative views of Polish-Ukrainian relations reach highest level on record in Poland

The proportion of Poles who hold a negative view of Polish-Ukrainian relations has risen to 46%, the highest figure ever recorded by Polish state research agency CBOS. Only 12% think relations are good. By contrast, three years ago, in mid-2023, only 3% had a negative view and 64% a positive one. Meanwhile, CBOS also found that belief among Poles that reconciliation between the two neighbours, who share a difficult history, is possible is at its lowest level on record, 53%, down from 78% three years ago. The findings follow other polls showing worsening attitudes towards Ukraine and Ukrainians in Poland in recent years, and come amid an ongoing diplomatic crisis triggered by President Volodymyr Zelensky naming a military unit after a group that massacred Poles in World War Two. Przekonanie o możliwości pojednania między Polakami 🇵🇱 a Ukraińcami 🇺🇦 spadło do najniższego poziomu w historii naszych pomiarów. 📙 Więcej w komunikacie #CBOS "Stosunki polsko-ukraińskie" ⤵️ https://t.co/kw2o4upY3Q#Ukraina #Ukraińcy pic.twitter.com/LItCFC3f2m — CBOS (@CBOS_Info) August 11, 2026 Relations between Poland and Ukraine improved significantly in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, as Poland welcomed millions of Ukrainian refugees and provided Kyiv with extensive military, humanitarian and diplomatic support. However, since 2023, those relations have been hit by a series of controversies over Ukrainian agricultural exports, border blockades by Polish farmers and truckers, and, above all, over the two nations’ difficult World War Two history. Among Poles who now hold a negative view of relations, CBOS also asked them who was responsible for the situation. A large majority, 65%, primarily blamed Ukraine, while only 4% said it was Poland’s fault and 28% placed responsibility on both sides. In its regular surveys since 1997, the agency has also asked Poles if they believe that reconciliation between Poles and Ukrainians is possible or not. In the early 2000s, that figure rose to a record level of 81%, and in 2023 it still stood at 78%. Now, however, it has dropped to an all-time low of 53%. There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over their difficult, intertwined histories, in particular during the first half of the 20th century. In World War Two, Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, in an ethnic-cleansing operation known as the Volhynia massacres. Poland has officially recognised that episode as a genocide. However, Ukraine rejects that label and also points to the persecution of Ukrainians who lived in the interwar Polish state, as well as to massacres of Ukrainians by Polish groups during World War Two. Long-simmering tensions between Poland and Ukraine over WWII massacres have finally boiled over, prompting a diplomatic crisis.@danieltilles1 looks at how we got here and what it may mean for the two countries and Europe more broadly https://t.co/a8tiYJJHRr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 22, 2026 Those tensions recently boiled over after Zelensky, in May this year, approved a request to rename a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”, the group that led the Volhynia massacres but is remembered positively in Ukraine for its role in fighting Moscow-imposed Soviet rule. Zelensky’s decision prompted his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki, to strip the Ukrainian president of Poland’s highest honour. While tensions have since calmed somewhat, the dispute remains unresolved. However, even before that diplomatic crisis broke out, polling showed increasingly negative attitudes in Poland towards both Ukraine and Ukrainians, who are by far the country’s largest immigrant group. In its annual survey of attitudes towards various national and ethnic groups, published in February, CBOS found that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians had increased by five percentage points year-on-year, to 43%. Only 29% said they liked Ukrainians. In January, CBOS reported that opposition to accepting Ukrainian refugees in Poland had risen to its highest ever level. In December 2024, a poll in Ukraine found that positive sentiment towards Poles had fallen by half in the space of two years. The proportion of Poles opposed to accepting Ukrainian refugees has reached its highest ever level of 46%, up from 3% in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion. Other recent surveys have also indicated declining sympathy towards Ukrainians among Poles https://t.co/DLPGY2ToZG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 7, 2026 Meanwhile, the number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland rose by 30% in the first half of 2026, including a number of high-profile incidents. Poland’s government has blamed increasing anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from the right-wing and far-right opposition. Last month, Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called on “Polish politicians to stop inciting hatred against Ukrainians”. CBOS’s new study shows that attitudes towards relations with Ukraine differ significantly depending on political affiliation. Whereas 35% of supporters of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO), Poland’s main ruling party, hold a negative view of relations, that rises to 52% among voters of the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party and 81% for the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). Among those with a negative view, 49% of KO voters blamed Poland and Ukraine equally for the situation while 10% blamed mainly Poland. By contrast, 86% of Confederation supporters and 82% of PiS supporters placed responsibility on the Ukrainian side. Demonstrations took place in 25 Polish cities on Sunday against the “growing wave of hate and violence” against Ukrainians, who are Poland’s largest immigrant group. World.title: Poland unveils first warship under major naval modernisation programme
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has unveiled its first frigate to enter service in decades at a ceremony in the Baltic Sea port of Gdynia, where the ship was constructed. The development marks a major milestone in a 15 billion zloty (€3.5 billion) programme to modernise the ageing Polish navy and strengthen NATO’s maritime defences. “Poland is becoming a maritime power in the Baltic Sea,” declared Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a ceremony to name the new ship, which he attended alongside opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki in a rare show of unity. Na terenie PGZ Stoczni Wojennej w Gdyni prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki, @PremierRP @donaldtusk oraz wiceministrowie @MON_GOV_PL @magdasobkowiak i @pawelbejda uczestniczą w uroczystości chrztu pierwszej jednostki programu „Miecznik”, fregaty wielozadaniowej – przyszłego ORP Wicher. pic.twitter.com/X2ftjoKTLZ — Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej 🇵🇱 (@MON_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The ORP Wicher, a medium-sized warship designed for escort, air defence and other fleet protection duties, is the first of three multi-role frigates based on Britain’s Arrowhead 140 design being built under Poland’s Miecznik programme, the largest modernisation project in the history of the Polish Navy. It is due to be launched on Thursday in a complex manoeuvre involving its transfer and controlled launch from a semi-submersible barge. Shipyard officials have described the operation as one of the most demanding engineering projects undertaken by Poland’s shipbuilding industry. The three frigates are intended to form the core of Poland’s surface fleet and will replace Poland’s two current Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigates, which were constructed in the 1970s and transferred from the US Navy in the years 2000 and 2002. Ahead of Wicher’s launch, leading Polish officials attended the naming ceremony in Gdynia, including Tusk and Nawrocki, who are normally bitter rivals but have sought to present a more united front when it comes to national defence. “There can be no arguments or disputes when it comes to our country’s security,” said Tusk, who declared that Poland was seeking to play a role in “determining not only its own future, but also the entire region and Europe”. Nawrocki, meanwhile, said that the modernisation of the Polish navy “sends a clear message that we will develop our armed forces in every theatre – on water, on land, and in the air”. Both leaders also hailed the fact that the new frigates are being built in Poland itself, helping bolster the Polish shipbuilding industry. Prezydent RP @NawrockiKn w #Gdynia: Życzę, abyście zawsze szczęśliwie wracali do portu, któremu na imię Polska. pic.twitter.com/hHia2sCZfn — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) August 12, 2026 The contract for the three frigates was signed in 2021 between Poland’s state Armament Agency (AU) and a consortium led by state-owned defence group PGZ, with British defence firm Babcock and other foreign partners also involved. The project was initially valued at about 8 billion zloty but had risen to around 15 billion zloty by the end of 2023 following amendments. Construction of the second frigate in Gdynia’s military shipyard began in May 2025, while work on the third began in April this year. The programme is scheduled to be completed by the end of 2031. Swedish defence giant Saab has signed a strategic collaboration agreement with Polish state defence group PGZ. Their missions will include protecting shipping lanes and critical energy infrastructure and taking part in NATO naval groups. In recent years, Poland has also increasingly oriented itself towards the Baltic region, forming closer economic, energy and military ties with allies around the sea. Last year, Poland and Sweden signed a strategic partnership on defence and economic ties. They subsequently held their first ever bilateral military exercises in the Baltic. World.title: Negative views of Poland’s justice system have grown under Tusk government, finds state pollster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The proportion of Poles who negatively assess their country’s justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law and ensure that courts function more effectively and independently. New polling by state research agency CBOS found that, in June this year, 61% of Poles had a negative view of the functioning of the justice system, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017, when the former Law and Justice (PiS) government was in power. Only 26% now positively assess the system, down from 28% in 2022 and 36% in 2017. The last time positive views were lower was in 2005 (22%). The findings come two and a half years after the current government, a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power in December 2023, replacing the national-conservative PiS administration. One of Tusk’s main promises was to restore the rule of law after eight years in which PiS had implemented a series of contested judicial reforms that experts, European courts and many Polish judges had condemned as undermining the independence and functioning of the judiciary. However, Tusk’s government has struggled to implement its promised changes. In many cases, its efforts have been blocked by PiS-aligned Presidents Andrzej Duda and Karol Nawrocki or other officials appointed under the former government. But in other cases, such as with a pledge to separate the functions of justice minister and prosecutor general, which were fused by PiS in 2016, the current ruling coalition has simply not followed through on its promises. In its latest polling, CBOS found that supporters of the current opposition are most dissatisfied with the functioning of the justice system: 72% of PiS voters have a negative view, as do 71% of those who support the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). However, even among voters of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, a majority, 53%, have a negative opinion, with only 38% holding a positive one. Interestingly, public attitudes towards judges themselves have hardly changed. Currently, 19% of Poles have a positive view towards them and 23% a negative one. That is similar to findings in 2017 (22% positive, 24% negative) and 2012 (19% positive, 23% negative). More Poles (35%) think that the rule of law has got worse under Tusk's government than believe it has improved (24%). A further 28% think there has been no change, finds a new poll https://t.co/KkiuY2vDSW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 5, 2025 When asked to identify the greatest problems with the justice system, Poles instead often point to structural issues – that is, those that are under the control of politicians. The most commonly identified problem (chosen by 38% of respondents, who could select up to three main problems) was “prolonged proceedings” in court cases. The second biggest issue was “politicisation of courts” (18%). Only 4% said that “judges’ neglect of duty, incompetence and impunity” were among the biggest problems. However, 23% of respondents were unable to name a single major issue that the justice system faces. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 CBOS’s findings echo a number of other polls. After the first year of Tusk’s government, a survey by SW Research for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 35% of Poles thought the rule-of-law situation had got worse, compared to only 24% who thought it had improved. Another poll by the same agency for Onet, a news website, in January this year similarly found that 40% of Poles believe the justice system has not improved under the current government, while only 33% think it has got better. In response to the latter poll, justice minister Waldemar Żurek admitted to Onet that there had been problems in addressing the rule of law. But he blamed the “hurdles [put] in our path” by Presidents Duda and Nawrocki. Opposition-aligned President @NawrockiKn has vetoed a government bill intended to reform a judicial body at the heart of Poland’s rule-of-law crisis. He argued that the measures would simply create even greater “legal chaos” https://t.co/I7FHRKIoP1 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 19, 2026 In 2024, Duda refused to sign government bills overhauling the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which still contains judges illegitimately appointed under the former PiS administration. As a result, Tusk’s government refuses to recognise rulings issued by the TK. In February this year, Duda’s successor, Nawrocki, vetoed a government bill intended to restore the legitimacy of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), the body responsible for nominating judges to positions on courts. In 2017, the KRS was overhauled under PiS in a manner that rendered it illegitimate, according to multiple Polish and European court rulings. That in turn has led to doubts over the legal status of around 3,000 judges appointed by the KRS since 2017 and all the rulings issued by them. Nawrocki has also refused to swear in four new TK judges nominated by parliament this year, despite an order by the European Court of Human Rights that they be allowed to take up their positions. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Indians and Colombians now third and fourth largest groups of foreign workers in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians. The figures also show that the overall number of registered foreign workers has risen more than 8% over the last year, a faster rate of growth than in recent years. However, the government official responsible for migration strategy says this is because stricter government measures have pushed some employers to register previously uninsured workers. The ZUS data, reported by Dziennik Gazeta Prawna (DGP), a leading daily, show that there were 1.34 million foreign workers registered in ZUS at the end of June, up from 1.24 million at the same point last year. That 8.2% increase is larger than the growth rate of around 6% seen in each of the previous two years, notes the newspaper. Maciej Duszczyk, the deputy interior minister responsible for migration, commented that the rise actually reflects the government’s tougher migration strategy, which he said “forces employers to report for insurance those who arrived earlier” but were working unregistered The official pointed to recent data showing that, in fact, in the first half of this year, Poland issued 50% fewer work permits to foreigners than in the same period of 2025. Dane ZUS pokazują dokładnie to co zakładaliśmy w Strategi Migracyjnej. Radykalny spadek liczby wydawanych, nowych zezwoleń na pracę (ponad 50% rok do roku) wymusza na pracodawcach zgłaszanie do ubezpieczenia, tych którzy przyjechali wcześniej. Tylko w pełni legalne zatrudnienie! — Maciek Duszczyk (@MaciekDuszczyk) August 11, 2026 Ukrainians remain by far the largest group of registered foreign workers, with 901,000 now in the system, a 10.1% rise from a year earlier. Belarusians (144,000, up 4.9%) remain in second. But two non-European migrant groups whose numbers have been growing rapidly in recent years now occupy third and fourth place: Indians (25,500, up 4.9%) and Colombians (23,000, up 31%, which was the fastest growth of any national group). Georgians, who had previously been the third-largest group, saw their number fall by 17% to 22,000, meaning they are now in fifth, ahead of Filipinos (15,400, down 2%), Moldovans (14,200, down 1%), Nepalis (13,400, up 8.3%), Vietnamese (12,200, up 6.1%), and Russians (11,800, down 2.5%). Latin American migration to Poland is booming, with 45,000 work permits issued last year, five times more than in 2022@Gosia_Tomczak looks at what is driving this trend and what challenges and opportunities it has created for both the migrants and Poland https://t.co/tl1wUTCaC0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2025 ZUS’s data also show that foreign workers are increasingly establishing their own businesses in Poland, which Dziennik Gazeta Prawna notes is a sign that they are establishing longer-term ties with the country but also a result of an easier online system for registering businesses. In 2021, only 22,700 foreigners had a registered business in Poland, a figure that now is now almost five times higher, at 102,000. The rise has been driven in particular by Ukrainians, many of whom are legally entitled to establish companies in Poland under the same terms as Polish citizens. As a result, 7.6% of foreign workers now run their own business, up from 6.7% a year ago and from 2.7% before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which led to a wave of Ukrainian refugees settling in Poland. Ukrainian refugees boosted Poland’s GDP by 2.7% last year while not raising unemployment or lowering wages, finds a report by the UN @Refugees agency and @Deloitte "Whoever thinks refugees are a burden on the economy should think again," says @UNHCRPoland https://t.co/rOvtOvBNwG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2025 Over the last decade, even before the war in Ukraine, Poland has experienced a wave of migration unprecedented in its history and among the largest anywhere in Europe. For six years running, between 2017 and 2022, it issued more first residence permits to immigrants from outside the European Union than did any other member state. Much of the surge in immigration came during the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government from 2015 to 2023, despite its strong anti-migrant rhetoric. The current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power pledging to reduce immigration, which it said had got out of control under PiS. Under Tusk’s government, in 2024, Poland issued the lowest number of residence permits to non-EU immigrants in a decade. In 2025, the government introduced tougher entry requirements for foreign workers and students. It has also stepped up deportations of foreigners who have broken the law. However, Duszczyk notes that the current government still sees “selective and responsible migration” as a way to “maintain the competitiveness of the economy without limiting wage growth”. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Mother bear and cubs spotted on busy hiking trail in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
