World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.content:
Union minister Kiren Rijiju targets opposition

Lok Sabha productivity at 19%, Rajya Sabha at 39%

Public Examinations Bill was discussed in both Houses

Opposition protests continued through the session

Rijiju targets Congress over disruptions

NEW DELHI: Parliamentâs Monsoon Session ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die, bringing to a close a session marked by repeated disruptions and protests by opposition parties.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the session was successful in terms of legislative business, with 12 Bills passed, but criticised the quality of debates and discussions.Addressing a press briefing, he said the government was not satisfied with the level of parliamentary discussion during the session.Rijiju said Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19% of the total allotted time, while Rajya Sabha recorded 39%.âThe Monsoon Session concluded today. We view it from two perspectives. In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful,â Rijiju said.He alleged that opposition parties repeatedly disrupted proceedings and avoided discussions offered by the government.âBased on my parliamentary experience and what I have seen in my life, this is the first time the Opposition was running away from discussions,â he said.According to Rijiju, 11 Bills were passed in the Lok Sabha without discussion, while one Bill underwent discussion. He said the Bills were discussed in the Rajya Sabha, although Congress and some other Opposition members staged a walkout.Rijiju said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill was the only legislation to undergo a full discussion in the Lok Sabha during the session.âOnly one bill, addressing the issue of paper leaks and unfair means in examinations, underwent a full discussion in the Lok Sabha,â he said.The legislation, which seeks to prevent unfair means in public examinations, was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha before being passed during the session.The Monsoon Session, which began on July 20, witnessed prolonged disruptions in both Houses.Opposition protests initially focused on the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The opposition later sought discussions on police action against students protesting over the NEET issue and demanded statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.The government offered a discussion on the NEET paper leak and related issues, along with a reply from Shah, but the proposal was rejected by the Congress. A similar proposal made on Wednesday also failed to break the deadlock.Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition wanted answers over allegations concerning police action against protesting students and criticised the prospect of a speech by Shah.Rijiju accused Congress MPs of reducing their parliamentary role to sloganeering and creating disruptions.âAnother observation I have made is that Congress MPs seem to believe their primary role is merely to raise slogans and create a ruckus with placards and banners,â he said.He also said disruptions had particularly affected newly elected MPs by limiting opportunities for debate and discussion.âAs the minister of parliamentary affairs, I feel genuinely sorry for the Congress MPs, especially the new ones,â Rijiju said. âHow can they learn if there are no debates or discussions?âHe expressed hope that opposition parties would reflect on their conduct and participate in more substantive debates when Parliament reconvenes for the Winter Session.The session also saw counter-protests between BJP and INDIA bloc MPs at the Makar Dwar steps of the Parliament complex.

World.title: 'Bid to weaken stir': Students accuse Jharkhand govt of withholding Devendra Mahto's health details
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, with protesting students alleging that the state government is withholding information about his health to weaken their agitation.

Meanwhile, former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital and enquired about his health.

Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge on August 10. The wider protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants entered its 20th day on Thursday, with students continuing their agitation at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

Students allege govt hiding Mahtoâs health details

The protesting students have alleged that the government is not allowing them to meet Mahto at the hospital and is withholding details about his health.

Mahto was moved to Sadar Hospital by the administration late Monday evening after police used force to disperse thousands of aspirants who had marched towards the state assembly.

Raghubar Das meets Mahto

In a post on X, Mahto said: "Former Chief Minister of Jharkhand Raghubar Das ji reached the hospital and inquired about my well-being, while also assuring support for our movement."

Das had on Wednesday threatened to go on a hunger strike if the demand for a CBI probe was not fulfilled within a week.





He has also sought compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of 19 people who died during the 2024 excise constable physical examination.

The BJP has accused the Hemant Soren government of suppressing the student movement, while the Congress has accused the saffron party of politicising the agitation and alleged that it brought workers from outside Jharkhand to disrupt the protests.

On Tuesday, in a message shared on social media, Mahto said "My body is undergoing treatment in the hospital bed, but my soul and resolve are at the Satyagraha site where students and youth are engaged in a just struggle for their future.

The indefinite hunger strike continues on its 11th day in Sadar Hospital."

Mahto has also sought permission from the hospital authorities to return to the protest site. In a handwritten application to the Civil Surgeon, he said being separated from the protesting students was causing him greater distress than his physical ailments.

He cited his responsibility towards thousands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and sought permission to rejoin them.

The protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. They have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the state government.

Jharkhand protest enters 20th day

The studentsâ agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations entered its 20th day on Thursday. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch has been demonstrating at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, demanding greater transparency in recruitment examinations, cancellation of several tests and an independent probe by the CBI or a panel of retired judges from outside Jharkhand.

Tensions escalated on Monday when JPSC and JSSC aspirants marched towards the state assembly. Police used batons, water cannons and tear gas to disperse the protesters.

Mahto was among those taken to hospital after the confrontation. He later sought permission to leave the hospital and return to the protest site, saying his presence with the students was important to the movement.

The ABVP has announced protests at more than 1,200 universities over the issue. Its leaders have also questioned the credibility of the state-appointed SIT into the alleged examination irregularities, citing repeated changes in its composition.

The protesters have so far refused to call off the agitation, maintaining that they will continue the movement until their demands are addressed.

World.title: UP Creators Summit & Awards to celebrate the state's rising digital voices and creator economy in grand 2-day event
World.content:
As India's creator economy continues to redefine entertainment, entrepreneurship and storytelling, Uttar Pradesh is emerging as one of the country's fastest-growing hubs for digital innovation.

With increasing internet penetration, a thriving startup ecosystem and the rapid rise of creators from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, the state is playing a pivotal role in shaping India's digital future.

Celebrating this transformation, the inaugural edition Times of Indiaâs UP Creators Summit & Awards will bring together some of the state's most influential content creators, industry leaders, brands and digital innovators for a 2-day mega showcase of recognition, insightful conversations and future-focused learning.

To be held on August 19 and 20 in Varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of Uttar Pradesh, the event will bring together the stateâs rich heritage and its new-age digital voices, showcasing how creators are shaping the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The first day, August 19, will feature insightful masterclasses, panel discussions and fireside chats, while August 20 will culminate in the grand UP Creators Awards, celebrating the stateâs most impactful digital creators.





Honouring the creators shaping a new Uttar Pradesh

At the heart of the event are the Creators Awards, which will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more. These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage.

The awards celebrate creators who are redefining digital influence while contributing to the state's growing reputation as a powerhouse of innovation and creativity.

Conversations driving the future of the creator economy

Beyond the awards, the summit will serve as a platform for thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges shaping the creator ecosystem.

Panel discussions will explore how the creator economy is expanding beyond metropolitan cities into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, the growing influence of creators in rebranding Uttar Pradesh, and the role of digital storytellers in building the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh.

The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session concludes: Key takeaways from the final day of proceedings
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Parliamentâs Monsoon Session concluded on Thursday with both Houses adjourned sine die after weeks marked by legislative business, opposition protests and repeated disruptions over the Jantar Mantar protest and other political flashpoints.

The Lok Sabhaâs final morning was strikingly brief. In just three minutes and 10 seconds, members assembled, all six stanzas of Vande Mataram were rendered, MPs including Prime Minister stood to attention, and Speaker Om Birla adjourned the House sine die.

The closing proceedings unfolded amid familiar slogans, with the Opposition shouting âapologise, apologiseâ and âwho ordered the lathi-charge?â as home minister

entered. Birla also skipped his customary valedictory remarks on the Houseâs performance, underscoring a session dominated by disruption.

Rajya Sabha witnessed Mallikarjun Kharge remarks over Haldwani 'Suddhikaran' row followed by JP Nadda's clarification and condemnation of the event.

Meanwhile, in Rajya Sabha, leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge raised the Haldwani âsuddhikaranâ row, alleging that a havan was conducted at the venue after his rally. Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the incident and assured Kharge that the matter would be investigated.





Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die

The Lok Sabha was adjourned sine die by Speaker Om Birla at 11.06 am, followed by the Rajya Sabha, bringing the 19-sitting Monsoon Session to an end. The session had been scheduled from July 20 to August 13. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju had said before the session that the government wanted the Houses to see âmeaningful debate, discussion and decisions on issues of National importanceâ.

The closing proceedings, however, came amid a continuing logjam over the oppositionâs demand for a government response to the police action against students protesting the NEET controversy.

Rijiju flags low Parliament productivity

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said 12 Bills were passed during the Monsoon Session, but acknowledged that parliamentary discussion remained limited. âIt was a good sessionâ¦we have passed 13 bills; but it was not a good session in terms of discussion,â he said. Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19%, compared with 39% in Rajya Sabha, he added. He also accused the Opposition of avoiding debate despite the governmentâs willingness to discuss issues.

Six stanzas of Vande Mataram played in Lok Sabha

On the last day of the Monsoon Session, Lok Sabha proceedings opened with all six stanzas of Vande Mataram on Thursday, marking a first for Parliament. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and other senior leaders were present. The move followed fresh Union home ministry directions on the National Songâs protocol. During the session, Parliament also passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, providing statutory protection around national symbols.

Kharge raises âpurificationâ row in Rajya Sabha

Congress president and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge used the final day to raise an alleged âpurificationâ ritual at the Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani after his public meeting there.

Kharge said, âI was in Haldwani where I made a public speech at Ramlila Maidan. Lakhs of people were there. At that time, I did not mention the name of any community or religion; I only reiterated the issues of the Govt.

But after my speech, people of BJP performed a âhavanâ there to âpurifyâ that stage...Is this the way in a democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution? I am the LoP.â

Union minister JP Nadda responded that the BJP did not support such an act and said it would be investigated. âBJP does not subscribe to such activities. Never. But we will investigate this. I assure you that whatever happened there will certainly be investigated,â Nadda said, adding that he condemned the incident.

Modi and Shah present as session closes

PM Narendra Modi and Union HM Amit Shah were present during the closing proceedings, as the student protest controversy remained the dominant unresolved political issue. The Opposition had demanded Shahâs statement and his presence in the Houses over the police action during the July 20 march by students towards Parliament.

On Wednesday, Shah said the government was prepared for a detailed discussion. âAs far as the discussion is concerned, Kiren Rijiju, who is our parliamentary affairs minister, has made it very clear that the government is ready to discuss every aspect of the student protests regarding NEET,â Shah said.

He added, âOn my part, I have also said that I am ready to answer any question in Parliament. But they don't want the discussion to happen at all. Now let the public decide who is running away.â

Rahul Gandhi rejected the offer, saying the Opposition was not interested in an âAmit Shah lectureâ and questioning who ordered the use of force against protesting students.

Bills: 12 introduced, 11 passed by both Houses

The Monsoon Session saw 12 Bills introduced, with 10 cleared by both Houses, according to PRS Legislative Research.

Key legislation covered public examinations, national honour, birth and death registration, the Supreme Court, MSMEs, taxation, tribunals, cooperative development, Keralaâs name and mining.

The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill received the most debate, 17 hours and 34 minutes across both Houses. Several other Bills passed with limited discussion, including four minutes each for the birth and death registration and Supreme Court judges Bills.

NEET protests and the political battle that dominated the session

The NEET controversy and police action against student protesters dominated the Monsoon Session, with the Opposition demanding a debate on alleged examination irregularities, education minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation and accountability for the July 20 crackdown. Repeated protests led to adjournments, while the government said it was ready for discussion.

The Opposition, however, linked any debate to accountability over the alleged police action. The issue remained unresolved at the sessionâs close. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi asked, âWho shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails?â

The wider legislative and political legacy

Beyond the NEET confrontation, the session produced a broad legislative package.

Parliament cleared the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, raising the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges other than the Chief Justice from 33 to 37; the MSME Development Amendment Bill; taxation amendments; the Tribunals Reforms Bill; the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill; the National Cooperative Development Corporation Amendment Bill and the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill.

The Kerala Bill was among the final measures passed, clearing the Lok Sabha on August 11 and the Rajya Sabha on August 12.

The Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill cleared the Rajya Sabha on the final day.

The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill became another major political flashpoint. Instead of being passed, it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for detailed scrutiny amid Opposition demands that it be withdrawn.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session ends amid disruptions; Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die amid repeated disruptions and political confrontations between the government and Opposition.

The session, which began on July 20, witnessed protests inside and outside the Houses over several issues, while Parliament also passed a number of legislations.

Rijiju says session successful in business, but debate fell short

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the Monsoon Session was successful in terms of legislative business but fell short on debate and discussion. He said Parliament passed 12 Bills during the session, but productivity remained low amid repeated disruptions.

"In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful," Rijiju said.

He said the Lok Sabha recorded 19 per cent productivity against the total time allotted, while productivity in the Rajya Sabha stood at 39 per cent. Rijiju attributed the lower productivity largely to disruptions by Opposition parties, while noting that NDA members and MPs from some Opposition parties participated in debates.





Rijiju said only one Bill in the Lok Sabha â the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, dealing with paper leaks and unfair means in examinations â underwent a full discussion. The legislation was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha.

He criticised the Opposition for not allowing debates to proceed, saying the government was ready to provide answers to questions raised by Opposition MPs. "This is not healthy for the parliamentary democracy," Rijiju said.

He also accused Congress MPs of focusing on slogans, placards and protests instead of parliamentary debate, and said he hoped there would be a change before the Winter Session.

"In the Lok Sabha, 11 bills were passed without discussion, while one underwent discussion," Rijiju said, adding that the concerned Bill was fully discussed in the Rajya Sabha.

Rajya Sabha skips question hour, passes Mines and Minerals Bill

The Rajya Sabha was adjourned sine die after chairman C P Radhakrishnan highlighted the performance of the House during the session.

Deviating from the normal pre-lunch schedule on the final day, the Upper House dispensed with the Zero Hour and Question Hour and took up the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill. The legislation was subsequently passed by a voice vote.

The Rajya Sabha had witnessed repeated disruptions during the session over issues including police action against students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak and allegations concerning the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

The House also witnessed a confrontation between leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and the government over an alleged 'Shuddhikaran' or purification ritual at a stage in Haldwani after Kharge addressed a Congress rally there on August 8.

Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, saying he had spoken about people's problems and had not mentioned any community or religion during his speech.

âBut after my speech, people associated with the BJP carried out a 'purification' ritual of that stage,â Kharge said, questioning whether such an incident was appropriate in a democracy.

Leader of the House JP Nadda said the BJP did not support such activities and assured the House that the allegation would be investigated.

âWhat Kharge ji has said is truly a matter of concernânot just for the Congress party, but for all of us,â Nadda said. âI want to make it absolutely clear that the BJP does not subscribe to such activities.â

Chairman C P Radhakrishnan said untouchability was condemned by all members and asked the government to investigate the allegation and punish those responsible if it was found to be true.

Lok Sabha ends amid opposition protests

The Lok Sabha was also adjourned sine die soon after proceedings began on the final day, following the traditional playing of Vande Mataram.

Proceedings were disrupted by Opposition MPs amid sloganeering, with political tensions also spilling into the Parliament complex.

BJP and opposition held counter-protests at the Makar Dwar steps, with the BJP protesting against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over the Congress' position on the ongoing protests in Jharkhand.

Opposition MPs, meanwhile, raised demands for the Union Home Minister to make a statement in the House and for the Prime Minister to respond to issues raised by them.

Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi accused the ruling party of preventing Parliament from functioning.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âIt is the ruling party itself that is preventing Parliament from functioning,â he said, arguing that the Opposition had been seeking discussions and responses from the government on issues including the Public Examinations Amendment Act.

Union minister Manohar Lal Khattar rejected the opposition's allegations and said Parliament could not function without discussion.

âThe Lok Sabha is a forum for discussion. There is no point in proceeding without discussion,â Khattar said. He added that the House was a platform for representatives from across the country and âdoes not belong to any single individualâ.

The session ended after weeks of political confrontation, with disruptions remaining a prominent feature of proceedings in both Houses.

World.title: Punjab governor recommends parole for convict Jagtar Singh Hawara in ex-CM Beant Singh assassination case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Thursday said he has recommended parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara, who is serving a life sentence for the assassination of former chief minister Beant Singh and had sought relief to meet his ailing mother.

His statement came a day after Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged Kataria to intervene and facilitate Hawaraâs parole.

Former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu, who is the former chief minister's grandson, had also called for Hawara to be granted parole. Beant Singh was killed in a suicide bombing in Chandigarh in 1995.

"His mother is unwell. We have recommended his case on humanitarian grounds,â Kataria told reporters.

The governorâs intervention was required as Hawaraâs parole plea is being considered in Delhi.

Earlier, Mann on Wednesday backed parole for Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying his ailing mother had a ârenewed hopeâ of meeting her son after 31 years.

The chief minister said Kataria, who is also the administrator of Chandigarh, had assured him that he would take up the matter with the Union home secretary. Mann had earlier written to Kataria, seeking 10-day parole for Hawara.





Bittu, meanwhile, expressed hope that the competent authorities would consider the request expeditiously and take an appropriate decision in accordance with law.

He reiterated that while his family would always honour the âsupreme sacrificeâ of Beant Singh, it also believed that compassion, humanity and peace should guide society forward.

Hawara was initially sentenced to death, but the sentence was later commuted by the high court. He is serving a life sentence in connection with the blast that killed Beant Singh and 16 others.

World.title: FSSAI proposes nutritional tables instead of warning labels on food packs
World.content:
Citing industryâs opposition to warning labels on food packets, the

(FSSAI) has suggested a tabular declaration of the recommended daily requirement of added sugar, saturated fats and salt.

The FSSAIâs affidavit filed in the Supreme Court only mentions the food industryâs opposition but has ignored the evidence in favour of warning label to help discourage consumption of foods high in added saturated fats, sugar and salt submitted by civil society representatives.

FSSAIâs âcomplianceâ affidavit in response to the Supreme Court order directing it to frame Front of Pack labelling regulation states that a âmajority of industry organizations were against the inclusion of âwarning labelsâ on the product,â and goes on to suggest a nutrition table giving âthe daily allowance for added sugar, added saturated fat and salt vis a vis their presence in per serve of packed food productâ on the front of the pack.

âThe proposed numerical table format being suggested by FSSAI would force consumers to do math at the supermarket shelf. The FSSAI has called it a âcomplianceâ affidavit but in reality, it is defiance. The Supreme Court had explicitly said that the exercise so far had not yielded any positive or good result and it had given FSSAI four weeks to revert. And six months later, FSSAI has filed an affidavit that abandons warning labels altogether and avoids defining HFSS (high fat, salt and sugar) foods.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Clearly, FSSAI has bowed to food industryâs interests,â said Dr Arun Gupta of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi).

FSSAI stated in the affidavit that it had held a stakeholder consultation on March 19, 2026 involving consumer groups, food industry representatives and farmer organisations. It stated that industry bodies argued that âconsumers should be able to make an informed decision without creating fear amongst the consumersâ. The affidavit was silent on the input given by consumer organisations, which had sought warning labels that have been shown to be the most effective in reducing consumption of junk food high in salt, sugar and saturated fats in several countries.

NAPi had also given FSSAI evidence generated from studies conducted in India and other countries showing how effective warning labels are.

World.title: Kerala vows strong opposition to Centre’s mining Bill amendment
World.content:
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Thursday (August 13, 2026) said the State government would mount strong political and, if necessary, legal opposition to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha a day ago.

He said the legislation amounts to “a serious encroachment on the State’s constitutional powers over land and poses a grave threat to India’s federal structure.”

Addressing mediapersons after the Cabinet meeting, Mr. Satheesan said the State’s principal objection was that the proposed amendment seeks to bring powers relating to land, a domain that comes under Entry 18 of the State List of the Indian Constitution, within the Centre’s sphere of authority.

He pointed out that the Constitution clearly distributes legislative powers between the Union, State and Concurrent Lists. While the Union has legislative authority over matters in the Union List, States have exclusive authority over subjects in the State List, and both have powers over subjects in the Concurrent List. Land, he pointed out, falls under Entry 18 of the State List and therefore comes within the legislative jurisdiction of the States.

He alleged that the Centre was attempting to expand its jurisdiction through the definition of “mineral-bearing land”, without even excluding coastal areas and forests. The State government will formally convey its protest to the Centre. It would also consider legal remedies if the Bill is ultimately passed and becomes law.

Vizhinjam port to begin EXIM cargo movement

Mr. Satheesan announced that direct export-import (EXIM) cargo movement at the Vizhinjam International Seaport will begin on August 18.

Vizhinjam has thus far been handling transshipment operations alone. Around 60% of the containers handled there have been containers originating from or destined for other countries.

The commencement of direct EXIM cargo movement will mark the first major milestone towards ensuring that the State begins to receive the direct economic benefits of the international port.

The Customs Commissionerate has already issued the necessary public notices for the commencement of EXIM cargo movement, he said.

A temporary road connection from the port road to national highway 66 has also been completed in accordance with the directions of the National Highways Authority of India. This arrangement has been put in place to facilitate cargo movement between the port and the national highway.

Mr. Satheesan added that the absence of an existing Container Freight Station facility in Thiruvananthapuram has necessitated an arrangement within the port itself. A Customs-bonded area has therefore been established inside the port, and the related work is progressing.

Aid for Wayanad landslide victims

The Cabinet also decided to provide an additional ₹2 lakh in financial assistance to all beneficiaries included in the Mundakkai-Chooralmala landslide rehabilitation list. He said the measure had been proposed earlier and that the government had now decided to implement it fully, with an expenditure of over ₹5 crore.

The Cabinet also decided to proceed with signing a memorandum of understanding (MoU) required for implementing the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban (PMAY-U) 2.0 through the Local Self-Government Department.

The Chief Minister informed that the Centre has placed certain conditions for the signing of the agreement. Among them is a requirement concerning the use of an emblem or logo associated with the scheme.

He said while there was no requirement to display a photograph of the Prime Minister, a logo or emblem specified as a condition by the Centre would have to be accepted when the MoU is signed.

The government has also issued guidelines for providing the bonus for the 2025-26 financial year to employees of public-sector institutions in Kerala.

World.title: Rajya Sabha Chairperson regrets disruptions during Monsoon Session; House productivity only 39%
World.content:
Rajya Sabha Chairperson C.P. Radhakrishnan on Thursday (August 13, 2026) expressed "deep concern" over disruptions that "derailed" the business of the House during the Monsoon Session.

As he adjourned the House sine die, he urged the members to uphold the dignity of the august House and discharge their parliamentary responsibilities in the highest traditions of Indian democracy.

Parliament Monsoon Session - key highlights

During the Monsoon Session that started on July 20, Mr. Radhakrishnan highlighted that 12 Bills were either passed or returned even as the productivity was only 39% because of disruptions.

"As the 271st Session of the Rajya Sabha draws to a close, I reflect on its proceedings with a deep concern. It is a matter of regret that the Session was marked by persistent disorder and frequent disruptions, which repeatedly derailed the business of the House," the Chairman said.

The loss of precious working hours also deprived the House of meaningful discussion and debate on matters of national importance, he added.

The Upper House saw several disruptions and adjournments as Opposition parties were protesting on several issues, including police action on students protesting against NEET paper leak and alleged theft of donations at Ram temple in Ayodhya.

Despite the disruptions, Mr. Radhakrishnan noted that the House managed to fulfil its core legislative duties by considering, passing or returning 12 Bills.

"Things would certainly have been different if we had collectively participated, contributed our valuable inputs and engaged in meaningful deliberations," he observed.

Elaborating on the performance, the Chairman said the House functioned for only 37 hours and 49 minutes, recording a productivity of 39.17%

As many as 285 Starred Questions were raised while there were 380 Zero Hour submissions and 380 Special Mentions. Only 16 Questions, 52 Zero Hour Submissions and 93 Special Mentions could be taken up.

Mr. Radhakrishnan rued that members did not make the fullest use of the opportunities to raise the voice of the people.

"As the House of Elders, this august Chamber has a unique responsibility to uphold reasoned debate, dignified dissent and thoughtful legislation. Repeated disruptions ultimately affect the trust and aspirations of the people. We must therefore strive to uphold the highest standards of parliamentary conduct and preserve the dignity and sanctity of this institution," he said.

The Chairman informed that an orientation programme was organised for the newly elected and nominated Members. The two-day programme provided valuable insights into parliamentary practice, procedure and the standards of conduct expected of Members.

As many as 35 Members attended the programme.

"I hope that when we meet again, we shall do so with a renewed resolve to uphold the dignity of this august House and discharge our parliamentary responsibilities in the highest traditions of our democracy, thereby strengthening our democratic institutions and our democracy at all times," Mr. Radhakrishnan said.

World.title: Abhimanyu murder case in Kerala: All 16 accused appear before court after reprimand
World.content:
All the 16 accused in the Abhimanyu murder case appeared before the Ernakulam Principal Sessions Court in Kerala on Thursday (August 13, 2026), after failing to be present during the last two hearings.

The court read out an additional charge of voluntarily causing hurt (Section 323 of the IPC) at the instance of the prosecution. Special Prosecutor G. Mohanraj appeared in the case.

Accused deny charge

The accused denied the charge. Principal Sessions Judge K. K. Balakrishnan subsequently posted the case for August 17.

The Kerala High Court had earlier directed that the trial be completed within four months, acting on a petition filed by the victim’s mother, Bhoopathy.

At the hearings on August 6 and August 10, the court had expressed strong dissatisfaction over the continued absence of the accused. On August 10, it dismissed their petitions seeking representation through lawyers. One of the reasons cited for seeking exemption from personal appearance was the alleged attempt to illegally capture images of the accused.

All 16 accused had pleaded not guilty when charges were initially read out on July 6, 2026. They face charges of murder, causing hurt with dangerous weapons, criminal intimidation, destruction of evidence, rioting, and unlawful assembly.

Earlier, the court had dismissed discharge petitions filed by six of the accused, ruling that sufficient grounds existed to proceed. The plea of the first accused seeking the return of the chargesheet was also rejected.

Abhimanyu, a second-year B.Sc. Chemistry student and SFI unit secretary at Maharaja’s College, was allegedly fatally stabbed on July 2, 2018, during clashes between activists of the SFI and the Campus Front, the student wing of the now-banned Popular Front of India (PFI), reportedly following disputes over graffiti. His murder triggered widespread protests and reignited debate over political violence on college campuses.

Although the police filed the chargesheet in September 2018, the trial was delayed due to a host of factors.

World.title: The long wait for a woman Minister in Karnataka
World.content:
The Karnataka Legislature’s monsoon session will begin on August 13 with an ignominious first in recent history: a Cabinet with not even a symbolic representation of women.

The last fortnight has been marked by endless squabbles over Cabinet expansion and portfolio allocation, with intense arguments on ways to ensure caste and regional representation. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and party functionaries have made multiple trips to New Delhi to consult with the high command, and spent much energy trying to placate “powerful” leaders who are miffed over being denied Cabinet berths or over not getting what are described as “plum portfolios.”

However, women’s representation has clearly not been regarded as an issue worth breaking a sweat over. When asked by the media why not a single woman was included in his 33-member Cabinet, Mr. Shivakumar candidly admitted that there was “no urgency” in the matter, while casually assuring that the one vacant place would be filled by a woman. In fact, it was in an equally casual manner that Gayathri Shanthegowda, the lone woman who was in the Congress high command’s approved first list of Ministers, disappeared before the swearing-in ceremony, as the urgent demands of other powerful interest groups took over.

This situation is nothing short of ironic for two reasons: Congress has nationally been vociferously arguing for 33% women’s reservation, without encumbering it with delimitation or any other riders. At the State level, the Congress government has come to power riding on the back of five guarantees, two of which are specifically aimed at women’s empowerment. While the Gruha Lakshmi scheme promises ₹2,000 a month to women heads of eligible families, Shakti offers free travel to women in select buses.

Symbolic representation

The signalling is that while women are very crucial as voters, they are the last priority when it comes to sharing political power. The final electoral rolls published ahead of the 2023 elections showed that women voters outnumbered men in 17 electoral divisions out of the 34 in Karnataka. Naveddu Nilladiddare, a network of feminists and women’s rights groups, in a letter to the Chief Minister, put it succinctly: “An all-male Cabinet is not an oversight. It is a political choice. It sends an unmistakable message that women and women’s leadership remain dispensable when it comes to the exercise of state power.”

Interestingly, while there have been multiple street protests by supporters of leaders demanding their induction into Cabinet — foregrounding their caste, region, seniority etc. — there were hardly any protests against the non-inclusion of women in the Cabinet. There was some feeble noise in Belagavi in north Karnataka over Lakshmi Hebbalkar, who handled the Women and Child Development portfolio under the Siddaramaiah-led government, being dropped, but none on the larger question of women’s representation. Brahmins not being represented in the Cabinet grabbed more attention than women being denied a place.

The history of electoral politics in Karnataka shows that women’s share in political representation has always been abysmal, much like the rest of the country. In the 2023 Assembly elections, out of a total of 2,613 candidates, 185 were women. Of them, 10 were elected (with one more added in bypolls), which constitutes about 4.5% of the total Assembly strength. In the first two elections in Karnataka in 1957 and 1962, the share of women’s representation stood at 6.25% and 8.65%, respectively, the latter being the highest ever. Since then, the share has fluctuated, with the 1972 election seeing not even a single woman elected to the Assembly out of the 28 who contested. This is all the more striking in a State which was a pioneer in giving 50% reservation to women in local bodies.

The representation of women in Ministry too has been symbolic across parties, with the highest being four when the late S.M. Krishna was the Chief Minister. Women are often given what are regarded as “light weight” portfolios such as Women and Child Development or Kannada and Culture.

No doubt Mr. Shivakumar will stick to his promise of filling the one vacant berth with a woman, but that will not go beyond what it has always been — a symbolic gesture — in the absence of a system that makes representation count.

World.title: Nurse found dead in N.R.S. Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata; probe ordered
World.content:
A female nurse was found dead inside the washroom of N.R.S. Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on late Wednesday (August 12, 2026), officials said.

The Kolkata Police has ordered a probe into the incident.

The 30-year-old nurse was on night shift at the hospital and had joined work on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) at around 8 p.m. Around two hours later, her colleagues could not locate her. Later they found her lying unconscious on the bathroom floor inside the hospital, the Kolkata Police officials said on Thursday (August 13, 2026).

She was declared dead after being shifted for medical treatment, according to the officials. “She was immediately shifted for medical treatment, where the attending doctor examined her and declared her dead. Upon thorough checking of the scene, no visible marks of injury and no suicidal note were found,” they added.

A post-mortem is being conducted to find out the real cause of death. Police are yet to determine if this was a case of death by suicide or there was any foul play involved.

Notably, two years ago on August 9, the discovery of a 31-year-old female doctor’s body at the R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital had taken the State by storm, raising several questions on the safety of medical staff inside hospitals, and safety of women at their workplace.

World.title: Kerala HC says it achieved a higher case clearance ratio
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has claimed to have achieved a significant increase in the number of matters available for hearing and disposal through the recently introduced Auto Cause List System (ACLS) and the campaigns undertaken by the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) to settle the cases.

The ACLS automatically identifies long-pending cases, prioritises them for listing before the appropriate Benches, and ensures regular and systematic listing of newly instituted cases. The campaign was led by Chief Justice Soumen Sen, according to a communication. Since its introduction on May 19, 2026, a total of 2,02,729 cases were listed before various Benches.

Of the 6,560 cases referred to the Kerala State Mediation and Conciliation Centre of the High Court from January to June 2026, as many as 724 cases were settled at the High Court and 18,110 cases in the district judiciary. The adalats conducted by the High Court Legal Services Committee and the National Lok Adalats organised across the State by the Kerala State Legal Services Authority (KeLSA) have settled 24,682 cases throughout the State. The High Court Legal Services Committee alone settled 70 cases in the High Court through the Adalats. The combined efforts of the agencies have helped the High Court achieve a higher case clearance ratio, according to a communication.

Victim compensation claims

KeLSA also facilitated the release of ₹48.23 crore for pending victim compensation claims across the State.

The scheme provides financial assistance to victims of crime, including women or their dependents, who have suffered loss or injury as a result of the crime and require rehabilitation, the communication said.

World.title: NDA, INDIA bloc MPs face-off outside Parliament over Jharkhand protest, Ram temple donation issues
World.content:
Ruling NDA and Opposition INDIA bloc MPs came face-to-face near Parliament's Makar Dwar on Thursday (August 13, 2026) — with security personnel forming a cordon between them — as they staged protests and raised counter-slogans over police action on job aspirants in Jharkhand and issues surrounding the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

While NDA MPs demanded answers from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and alleged that he was "running away" from a debate on student protests across the country, INDIA bloc MPs demanded accountability from Union Home Minister Amit Shah over alleged police excesses during the July 20 student protests over paper leaks.

The INDIA bloc MPs also raised the issue of alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

Before the face-off, the NDA MPs and the INDIA bloc MPs held their respective protests separately.

The NDA MPs sat on the steps of the Makar Dwar and raised slogans against Mr. Gandhi and accused him of running away from a debate on student protests in Jharkhand.

Also Read : Parliament Monsoon Session LIVE

Opposition MPs demanded accountability from Mr. Shah over alleged police excesses against students during their Parliament march over the NEET paper leak issue.

Carrying placards, the MPs stood in front of the Makar Dwar and raised slogans such as "Amit Shah maafi maango", "chanda chor, gaddi chhorh" and "Chanda chor, kahan milenge, BJP ke daftar mein".

The Opposition MPs, mostly from the Congress, the Samajwadi Party and the TMC, lined up behind a big banner that read "Chanda kisne loota hai?" and raised slogans against the BJP.

INDIA bloc MPs have been protesting for about three weeks, demanding Mr. Shah's presence in the House and a statement from him.

The government's offer for a debate and Mr. Shah's reply failed to end the stalemate, with the Congress insisting that the Home Minister's response should specifically address who ordered the firing of pellets against students.

The Congress had asserted that the demand for a discussion on the alleged theft of funds at the Ram temple is "non-negotiable".

World.title: 'A service to the world': Norwegian minister praises Pakistan's leadership for US-Iran mediation efforts
World.content:
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide reiterated his country’s appreciation of Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing US-Iran conflict on Thursday, saying it was a “service to the world and, hence, also to us”.

Eide, who is on a two-day visit to Pakistan, expressed these views while addressing a press conference alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad.

“I also really want to reiterate our strong support for the very important role that Pakistan has taken in this dramatic war that started on February 28 with the US-Israel attack on Iran,” he said, recalling that Norway was one of the Western countries that was “clearest and earliest” in stating that the war was a violation of international rules.

“If we stand up for international law, it has to apply to everyone, everywhere, all the time,” he stressed.

He said that while Norway had “significant disagreements with Iran on other issues, they also have the right to be protected as a state”.

Coming to Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing conflict, he said he realised how difficult mediation and facilitation of parleys between the two sides could be.

“I know what a massive task you were taking on when you offered Islamabad not only as the venue but also as the facilitator of these talks,” he said, lauding Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership for their efforts.

“What you have been doing is really a service to the world, and hence, also to us.”

The Norwegian foreign minister said Pakistan’s mediation efforts also mattered to his country as it was a large shipping nation.

“We share an interest in open sea lanes and the ability to trade in the high seas, and to respect the Constitution of the Oceans […] Whatever emerges from this tragic and unnecessary war in Gulf, we need to protect the principle of the free passage,” he explained. “And I am so happy we see completely eye to eye [on this],” he remarked.

The visiting minister added that his message to “anyone involved out there in the conflict is that this issue of free passage and an open strait is not an issue for the warring parties alone. It is a global issue that we have a shared interest in promoting”.

He said he had discussed other regional issues during the visit as well, ranging from the Kashmir issue to Afghanistan.

Moreover, Eide said, he was glad to learn more about a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia in Makkah.

“These are three countries with whom Norway has very good and close relations,” he noted.

At the outset of his address, Eide said he was honoured to be in Pakistan, saying the last time a Norwegian foreign minister visited Pakistan was 10 years ago.

“So it was about time,” he remarked. “I promised you many months ago that I would come, and today, I live up to my promise. I was looking forward to this visit, which is short but very effective.”

Eide said there was a “strong partnership” between Norway and Pakistan, as well as the people of the two countries.

“We have a sizable diaspora of Pakistani descent […] Many of them are in key positions of politics and society and are a very welcome contribution to our country; and the fact that we have so many people who know these two countries intimately is yet another argument for strengthening our economic ties,” he added.

The Norwegian foreign minister further said that Oslo and Islamabad were discussing strengthening economic ties “in the context of specifics” and enhancing trade ties in more structural ways.

Delegation-level talks

Eide had commended Islamabad’s mediation efforts after his arrival in the federal capital earlier in the day and as he held delegation-level talks with Dar, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

The visiting dignitary recognised Pakistan’s role as “important and constructive”, the FO said.

“The Norwegian foreign minister commended Pakistan’s important and constructive role during the recent Iran-US conflict, including the leadership and contributions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, DPM Dar and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir,” it said.

Both sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries, it added.

The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said.

The FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

In televised remarks, Eide appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties.

He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries.

“There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said.

Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan.

He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations.

Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership, including the prime minister and foreign minister, in efforts to promote peace in the Middle East.

Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved.

“I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said.

Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington.

“Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said.

He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population.

He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties

Earlier, the two ministers held a “restricted-format meeting”.

“DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” it said.

Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation.

The visit is the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade, the FO said, adding that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April, and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

World.title: Body of missing Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi recovered on Broad Peak
World.content:
The body of Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, who was among the 10-person expedition that went missing after the deadly Broad Peak avalanche, was recovered and shifted to the mountain’s base camp, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Thursday.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. Purja’s company later confirmed there were no survivors .

The bodies of seven climbers were found. However, the search for Sakhi, American climber Sarah Mallory Geis, and Nepalese climber Nawang Thindu Sherpa was suspended last week due to a risk of fresh avalanches.

On Thursday, ACP member Naila Kiani said that Sakhi’s body had been found. According to Naila, a team of local volunteers from Shigar, searching the area on their own initiative, found the remains, which were subsequently confirmed as those of Sakhi.

She said the volunteers — Muhammad Nadeem, Muhammad Bashir and Abuzar — first spotted the body and alerted others in the area. They, along with other volunteers, brought the body down from Camp 1 to the base camp.

ACP General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the body had been shifted to the Broad Peak Base Camp and would be airlifted to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters, weather permitting.

He said the bodies of two remaining climbers have not yet been recovered. Shigri said rescue efforts for the remaining climbers would resume once weather conditions improved and the area was deemed safe.

He said the local volunteers located Sakhi’s body at an altitude of 5,600 metres.

World.title: SHC orders formation of committee to probe HIV outbreak among children at Karachi hospital
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) directed the provincial government on Thursday to constitute a committee for an “independent, impartial and comprehensive” inquiry into the HIV outbreak among children at Karachi’s Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital.

A two-member SHC bench, headed by Justice Adnanul Karim Memon and comprising Justice Muhammad Jaffer Raza, issued the directive as it announced its reserved judgement on a plea seeking an independent inquiry, registration of a case and lifelong medical treatment as well as appropriate compensation for the affected children.

The outbreak was initially reported late last year, following which the Sindh government carried out screening at the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run hospital located in Karachi’s SITE area. According to data shared by the Sindh government, at least 78 children have been found infected with HIV at the hospital while a screening in the nearby area also confirmed 120 additional cases.

But Advocate Tariq Mansoor, the lawyer who moved the SHC on the matter, claimed in his petition filed in May that the total number of infected children is around 200.

The court observed in its order on the plea that the departmental proceedings and reports submitted so far had been “insufficient to determine the number of affected persons, the source and circumstances of transmission, compliance with infection-control protocols and the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, as well as the supervisory and individual responsibility of the officials concerned”.

Keeping this in view, the court deemed it necessary “in the interest of justice, transparency and public confidence that an independent fact-finding mechanism be constituted by the competent authority, without expressing any final opinion regarding the guilt or innocence of any individual”.

It directed that a committee, headed by the Sindh chief secretary, be constituted. The chief secretary should co-opt two senior officers not below the rank of BS-20 and “preferably having no direct administrative involvement in the affairs of the hospital or the proceedings under inquiry” to join the committee, the court order stated.

The court directed that the committee should determine:

The actual number and particulars of children and other patients who were found HIV-positive and who received treatment at the hospital during the relevant period

The source, circumstances and possible mode of transmission of HIV, based on available medical and scientific evidence
